title: திருமால் (1, 2)
theme: Paripadal 1 and 2, to Thirumal: the god in the fused forms of Balarama and Krishna, his ornaments and his war on the Danavas, his unknowability and identity with all things, the ages of the world in the order of the elements, the boar, the rank of the two brothers left open, the sacrifice as his food, and prayers to dwell at his feet with kin and to keep a mind without crookedness.
source_issues: Paripadal 1: the colophon names no poet, composer or pan (flag); the subject is திருமால்.
Paripadal 1 line 17: மணியொடும் has its vowel sign restored by rule (யடு/ளடு to யொடு/ளொடு); sangamtamil.com does not confirm it here (flag).

Paripadal 1 lines 20-21: நவையினிற் / றுணி divides one word across the line break, and line 16 (திரடெரி) and line 25 (வயிறிரிய) are printed with sandhi unsplit; the dense run of lines 14 to 28 is hard to segment.
Paripadal 1 line 13 and Paripadal 2 line 57 are the same line (flag): a refrain of the Thirumal songs, not a copying error.
Paripadal 2 lines 2 and 72 have gaps in the source (lacunae); the opening clause and the deed of lines 69 to 72 cannot be fully construed.
Paripadal 2 lines 52 and 61: flagged for a dropped heading line; read by eye, the text runs on without a visible gap at both points (51 to 52 and 60 to 61).

Paripadal 2 line 1 differs strongly from sangamtamil.com's text and lines 19, 20, 29, 37 and 40 are not in it; ours kept (flags). Lines 7 and 8 were repaired and line 35 has a vowel sign restored by rule (flags).
Paripadal 2: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; the pan பாலையாழ் is a musical mode, not a thinai.

tamil: மாயுடை மலர் மார்பின், மை இல் வால் வளை மேனிச்
சேய் உயர் பணைமிசை எழில் வேழம் ஏந்திய,
வாய் வாங்கும் வளை நாஞ்சில், ஒரு குழை ஒருவனை;
சேவல் அம் கொடியோய்! நின் வல வயின் நிறுத்தும்
நா வல் அந்தணர் அரு மறைப் பொருளே.
reading: The song opens on two forms of Thirumal: first the one with the thousand awful hooded heads spitting fire rising over his crown, a body white as a flawless conch, the plough with its curved mouth and a single earring; then the one with eyes like clustered fire-flowers, a body like the opened kaaya bloom, Tiru seated on his chest among bright jewels and a golden garment like fire running over a great hill, lord of the male-bird banner, whom the eloquent brahmins' rare scripture tells of.
nuance: The first five lines carry Balarama's emblems (the serpent hood, the conch-white body, the plough, the one earring) and the next five Krishna's (dark kaaya colour, Tiru on the chest, the golden garment), yet all are addressed to one god in the second person singular (ஒருவனை, கண்ணை, மேனியை): the poem fuses the two brothers into a single object of praise. The thing raised on the tall staff in line 4 (வேழம்) is not secure: elephant or reed; the known banner of the plough-bearer is the palmyra.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god by his forms and emblems: கடவுள் வாழ்த்து under paadaan (porul 2.27)

tamil: இணைபிரி அணி துணி பணி எரி புரை
விடர் இடு சுடர் படர் பொலம் புனை வினைமலர்
நெரி திரடெரி புரை தன மிகு தன முரண் மிகு
நெறி செறி வெறி உறு முறல் விறல் வணங்கு அணங்கு வில்
தார் அணி துணி மணி வெயில் உறழ் எழில் புகழ் அலர் மார்பின்
எரி வயிர நுதி எறி படை எருத்து மலை இவர் நவையினிற்
றுணி படல் இன மணி வெயில் உறழ் எழில் நக்கு
இமை இருள் அகல முறு கிறுகு புரி ஒரு புரி நாள்மலர்
மலர் இலகின வளர் பரிதியின் ஒளி மணி மார்பு அணி
மணம் மிக நாறு உருவின விரை வளி மிகு கடு விசை
உடுவுறு தலை நிரை இதழ் அணி வயிறிரிய அமரரைப்
சிரம் உமிழ் புனல் பொழிபு இழிந்து உரம்
உதிர்பு அதிர்பு அலம் தொடா அமர் வென்ற கணை.
reading: In a dense run of compounds the poet piles up the god's ornaments: worked golden flowers, gems from the wilds strung with pearls, a garland on a famed chest bright as sunlight, a fire-pointed weapon, and the arrow that won the war against the Danavas who rose roaring to fight the gods until their heads poured blood like a stream.
nuance: Lines 14 to 28 are written for sound more than syntax, in short chiming words (இணைபிரி அணி துணி பணி எரி புரை; நெறி செறி வெறி உறு முறல் விறல்), a sung, metrical display that suits a song set to music; the grammar of the run can be guessed but not fixed, and the reading above gives only its gist. The sentence closes on the single word கணை, the arrow, at line 28.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's ornaments and his victory over the Danavas, praise under paadaan

tamil: இன்னன் என்று உரைத்தல் எமக்கு எவன் எளிது?
திரு மறு மார்ப! நீ அருளல் வேண்டும்.
reading: Hailing the faultless lord who broke the pride of those who said 'we will fight', the father of two, Maal with shining jewels, the poet says that even sages of clear inquiry can hardly know his coming, so how could it be easy for us to say he is such and such; knowing how hard it is, yet driven by longing, he asks the god with Tiru's mark on his chest not to scorn as weak the words we speak here, but to grant grace.
nuance: The ineffability is argued a fortiori: if sages free of confusion (மருள் அறு தேர்ச்சி முனைவர்) cannot know him, singers cannot; the hymn then asks pardon for itself, so that the praise in the following lines is offered as acknowledged inadequacy. Who the two are whose father he is (இருவர் தாதை) is not said in the poem.

thinai_evidence.note: an address to the god asking grace, praise under paadaan

tamil: விறல் மிகு விழுச் சீர் அந்தணர் காக்கும்
திறன் இலோர்த் திருத்திய தீது தீர் சிறப்பின்
அம் கண் ஏர் வானத்து அணி நிலாத் திகழ்தரும்
ஐந் தலை உயிரிய அணங்குடை அருந் திறல்
நலம் முழுது அளைஇய புகர் அறு காட்சிப்
reading: The poet tells the god what he is: the aram that the great brahmins guard and the tenderness shown to those who love him, the valour that set right the faithless and the terror of his foes, the moon shining in the lovely sky and the burning sun, the mighty one of the five upraised heads and the lion, the sense-field of flawless vision with the flower and its scent, the rising cloud, the vast sky, the earth and the tall Himalaya.
nuance: Every line ends on நீ (you): this is identity, not likeness, and no comparison marker appears. The pairs are built as a king's praise is built (grace to friends and terror to foes, moon and sun), but cosmic items follow the moral ones, so that aram and the Himalaya are predicated of the god in the same breath. ஐந் தலை and மடங்கல் are not secure: the five-headed one may be the serpent or a god, and மடங்கல் may be the lion or the fire of the world's end.

thinai_evidence.note: the god praised as all things: paadaan

tamil: பொன் அணி நேமி வலம் கொண்டு ஏந்திய
யாம் இயைந்து ஒன்றுபு வைகலும் பொலிக! என,
reading: Therefore, since we see no one here of whom to say 'you are like these, you are such', and since he is the first of all lasting lives who holds the gold-adorned discus, the god is like only himself; his forms have fame like his, garments like gold, the bird banner, the twisted conch, the discus that killed the scornful, bodies like a washed gem and fame past counting; and so, the poet says, we, of joyful and secure heart, with our dear kin, pray to dwell together at your feet and prosper every day, worshipping the shade of your feet, poet of the true word.
nuance: The hymn ends its search for a likeness by comparing the god to himself (நின்னோர் அனையை, நின் ஒக்கும் புகழ்): a poetics built on comparison turns the device on its own subject and finds no vehicle. The attributes of lines 58 to 63 are in the plural (நிழலவை, உடையவை, கொடியவை), as if of his many forms. The god is finally named a poet (வாய்மொழிப் புலவ), the author of the true word, the singers' own calling raised to him. The prayer asks for life together with kin (சுற்றமொடு), not for release.

thinai_evidence.note: the closing prayer of a hymn: paadaan

reading: The poet tells the ages of the world in order: when the golden world and the earth went to waste and age upon age passed in the sky, came the age of the formless one that appeared as sound in the sky where the embryo grew, the age of the driving wind, the age of blazing red fire, the age of dew and cold rain, and within them, after flooding and filling and gathering again, the age of the great earth; past the counts named by numbers, the god made known one age, named for the boar's form, so that no one knows ages enough for his age, and the poet worships him, lord of the discus.
nuance: The ages follow the order of the elements: sky (as sound), wind, fire, water, earth, each born of the one before, a cosmogony told as history. நெய்தல், குவளை, ஆம்பல், சங்கம், கமலம், வெள்ளம் in lines 13 and 14 are not flowers here but the names of vast numbers, the counts by which ages are reckoned; they are therefore left out of karu. Line 2 is broken in the text, so the opening clause is incomplete.

thinai_evidence.note: the god praised as older than the ages: paadaan

tamil: இந் நிலைத் தெரி பொருள் தேரின், இந் நிலை
நின் நிலைத் தோன்றும் நின் தொல் நிலைச்சிறப்பே.
ஓங்கு உயர் வானின் வாங்கு வில் புரையும்
பூண் அணி கவைஇய ஆர் அணி நித்தில
செய்யோள் சேர்ந்த நின் மாசு இல் அகலம்-
வளர் திரை மண்ணிய கிளர் பொறி நாப்பண்
வை வால் மருப்பின் களிறு மணன் அயர்பு
reading: To those who say he is younger than the pure white one like a conch, the god is younger, and to those who call him elder to the lord of the palmyra banner with the dark garment, he appears elder; he is the centre of the flawless scripture studied by men of spotless rule, and whoever inquires into this finds his ancient greatness in his present state; his stainless chest, where the red goddess dwells like the spot on the moon amid ornaments curved like the rainbow and pearl garlands, is praised, and so is the deed of the white-tusked one who wedded the earth amid the waves, so that no word of those who think on it can mark it.
nuance: Both halves of lines 20 to 23 name the same brother, Balarama (white like conch; the palmyra banner), so the poet does not decide between the traditions that make Thirumal his younger or his elder: the god takes the rank the worshipper gives him. In line 30 the chest is the moon and the goddess on it its dark mark, a figure that turns the Srivatsa mark into a moon spot. Lines 32 to 35, on the boar and the earth, are hard to construe.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's greatness and his chest praised: paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the goddess on the god's chest

tamil: ஒடியா உள்ளமொடு உருத்து, ஒருங்கு உடன் இயைந்து,
கொடி அறுபு இறுபு, செவி செவிடு படுபு,
நனி முரல் வளை முடி அழிபு, இழிபு,
ஒருங்கு உருண்டு, பிளந்து, நெரிந்து, உருள்பு சிதறுபு,
போர் அடு குரிசில்! நீ ஏந்திய படையே:
பொன் ஏர்பு அவிர் அழல் நுடக்கு அதன் நிறனே.
reading: Those who rose together in fury, unbending, roaring against the thunder and swift as the wind, had their banners broken, their ears deafened, their crowns shaken and their footing lost, their loud conches and crowns destroyed, and their heads, garlands and all, rolled down, falling at once like countless clusters from tall dark palmyras torn up root and trunk, rolling, split, crushed and scattered, pouring mire till the earth sank: such is the weapon the god bears, which takes the lives of foes; his body is the Death that devours his enemies, and its colour is a flickering flame shining like gold.
nuance: The long simile of the uprooted palmyras is built in the same breathless chain of verbal participles (ஒருங்கு உருண்டு, பிளந்து, நெரிந்து, உருள்பு சிதறுபு) as the fall of the enemies, so sound and sense fall together. The god's body is not likened to Death but called it (கூற்றம் உடலே), the strongest form of puram praise turned on a god.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's weapon and victory in battle, praise under paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the god's body to his foes

tamil: நின்னது திகழ் ஒளி சிறப்பு இருள் திருமணி;
கண்ணே, புகழ்சால் தாமரை அலர் இணைப் பிணையல்;
நா வல் அந்தணர் அரு மறைப் பொருளே:
reading: The poet gives what the eloquent brahmins' rare scripture says of the god: his shining light is the dark sapphire, his eyes a pair of blooming lotuses, his truth the bright day, his patience the great earth, his grace the full sky; he is like that and the others, and he is also this and the one in every place, lord of the high banner of the red-beaked eagle.
nuance: Lines 58 and 59 work with the Tamil pointing letters: அவ்வும் (that, the far), உவ்வும் (this, the near) and எவ்வயினோயும் (whichever place): the god is whatever any demonstrative can point to. Line 57 repeats Paripadal 1 line 13 word for word, a fixed refrain of the Thirumal songs.

words: நா வல் அந்தணர் அரு மறைப் பொருளே
thinai_evidence.note: the god praised as all things, paadaan

tamil: படி நிலை வேள்வியுள் பற்றி ஆடு கொளலும்,
புகழ் இயைந்து இசை மறை உறு கனல் முறை மூட்டித்
திகழ் ஒளி ஒண் சுடர் வளப்பாடு கொளலும்,
தலை உற வணங்கினேம், பல் மாண் யாமும்;
reading: The teacher's words told in the scripture, the seizing of the goat in the sacrifice of the proper order, and the kindling of the fire by the chanted rite to take the abundance of its bright flame are food that comes with the god's own form, the coming that the brahmins see as equal to him, which others will not accept; to him who sealed the nectar in and went for the immortals, giving them unaging tradition and unceasing strength, the poet and his many kin bow their heads at his feet, praise and bless him with quiet hearts, and pray: may our understanding never know crookedness.
nuance: The animal of the sacrifice (ஆடு) is counted among the god's food without hesitation; the hymn sides with the brahmins' rite against those who do not accept it (பிறர் உடம்படுவாரா), a hint that the rite already had dissenters. The closing prayer asks not for wealth or release but for a mind without crookedness (கொடும்பாடு). Line 72 is broken, so the deed of lines 69 to 72 cannot be fully construed.

thinai_evidence.note: the god as the recipient of the sacrifice, and the closing worship: paadaan

title: திருமால் (3)
theme: Paripadal 3, to Tirumal: all classes of being spread out from the god, the Veda's praises of the bird, the boar and the swan, the uncounted hands and forms that only he can know, the lord of both gods and asuras for whom there is no enemy or friend, the god as the essence of each thing ruling the worlds with grace as umbrella and aram as sceptre, and a closing litany of names.
source_issues: Paripadal 3: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; பாலையாழ் is the pan, a musical mode, not a thinai.

Paripadal 3 line 32: a line flagged as dropped for a modern heading (கூந்தல் என்னும் பெயரொடு கூந்தல்) reads as verse: it would supply the object of எரி சினம் கொன்றோய் (the slaying of the demon named for hair), so our text likely lacks a genuine line here; line 31 (வடிவு வேற்றுமையும் பெயர் வேற்றுமையும்) also reads like a heading but is kept as verse.
Paripadal 3 lines 5 and 54 differ strongly from sangamtamil.com (தாளும், தோளும், எருத்தொடு பெரியை; சூர் மருங்கு அறுத்த சுடர்ப் படையோயே); ours kept.
Paripadal 3 lines 16 and 17 repeat a half-line (பயந்தோள் இடுக்கண் களைந்த புள்ளி-); it reads as deliberate chaining, not a copying error.
Paripadal 3 lines 62, 77, 83 and 94 are hard to construe in our text.

tamil: மறு பிறப்பு அறுக்கும் மாசு இல் சேவடி
தீ வளி விசும்பு நிலன் நீர் ஐந்தும்,
நீ‘ என பொழியுமால், அந்தணர் அரு மறை.
reading: The poet hails the dark one whose flawless red feet cut off rebirth and says that the five elements, the sun and moon, aram, the sons of Diti and of Vidhi, the eight, the eleven, the two, Dharma, the lion and the three-times-seven worlds with all that lives in them have been told as things spread out from him, as the unfailing true word declares; the rare Veda of the brahmins pours forth that he is both the one born in the lotus and that one's father.
nuance: The catalogue of lines 4 to 9 lists cosmic classes by number (the eight, the eleven, the two) without naming them, as a hearer who knew the list would supply them; the poet does not claim to see this himself but reports it as what the Veda says (lines 11 and 14), so the hymn's authority is borrowed from the brahmins' scripture. Line 5 differs strongly from sangamtamil.com's text.

words: மறு பிறப்பு அறுக்கும் மாசு இல் சேவடி
thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god as the source of all, sung as கடவுள் வாழ்த்து under paadaan

tamil: நிவந்து ஓங்கு உயர் கொடிச் சேவலோய்! நின்
மாசு இல் ஆயிரம் கதிர் ஞாயிறும், தொகூஉம்
ஊழி ஆழிக்கண், இரு நிலம், உரு கெழு
நால் எண் தேவரும் நயந்து நிற் பாடுவோர்
reading: The poet gives the praises the gods sing: you are the bird that seized the nectar from the jewelled immortals and ended its mother's distress, lord of the tall banner of that bird; who does not worship your red feet, the foot that reached the seven lower worlds; when fire, death, Yama and the thousand-rayed sun gathered in the sea at the age's end you ploughed up the great earth with a boar's tusk, and when the waters of the sky dried you dried your wings as a swan; our song follows the way those singers sing.
nuance: Lines 16 and 17 repeat the same half-line (பயந்தோள் இடுக்கண் களைந்த புள்ளின்), a chaining device that turns the bird first into the god himself and then into his banner. The boar and swan deeds are put in quotation as the gods' own hymn (எனவும் ... எனவும், lines 24, 26), and the poet then claims only to sing in their manner, so the human song is modelled on a heavenly one.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's deeds recited as worship: paadaan

tamil: எரி சினம் கொன்றோய்! நின் புகழ் உருவின, கை;
நடுவுநிலை திறம்பிய நயம் இல் ஒரூ கை,
முக் கை முனிவ! நாற் கை அண்ணல்!
ஐங் கைம் மைந்த! அறு கை நெடு வேள்!
பதிற்றுக் கை மதவலி! நூற்றுக் கை ஆற்றல்!
இனைத்து என எண் வரம்பு அறியா யாக்கையை!
நின்னைப் புரை நினைப்பின் நீ அலது உணர்தியோ,
reading: Your forms and names differ, slayer in burning anger, and your hands take the shape of your fame: the one hand without fairness that mixed the nectar and swerved from even-handedness, then two hands, three, four and on through ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand and a hundred thousand, and more than these, a body whose count no number bounds; if one thinks of something like you, who but you could know it, first of the ancient word, whose beauty in learning, strength, mind and perception knows no limit?
nuance: The first hand in the count is a reproach, not a praise: the hand that dealt out the nectar unfairly (lines 33 and 34) remembers the god's partiality to the gods against the asuras, which the next unit seems to answer by making him first of both. ஆம்பல் in line 44 is most likely the name of a very large number, not the water lily. The object of எரி சினம் கொன்றோய் (line 32) is missing; see source_issues.

thinai_evidence.note: praise by the uncountable forms of the god: paadaan

tamil: அணி நிழல் வயங்கு ஒளி, ஈர்-எண் தீம் கதிர்,
அணி மணிப் பைம் பூண், அமரர்க்கு முதல்வன் நீ;
திணி நிலம் கடந்தக்கால், திரிந்து அயர்ந்து, அகன்று ஓடி,
நின் அஞ்சிக் கடற் பாய்ந்த பிணி நெகிழ்பு அவிழ் தண் தார்
அன்னவர் பட, அல்லா அவுணர்க்கும் முதல்வன் நீ;
ஆயிர அணர் தலை அரவு வாய்க் கொண்ட
ஏஎ இன கிளத்தலின் இனைமை நற்கு அறிந்தனம்;
reading: You are first of the immortals, who wear gem-set ornaments and feed on the moon of sixteen sweet rays as it waxes from crescent to full, and you are first also of the asuras who, when you strode across the earth, turned, fainted, fled and leapt into the sea in fear of you, their cool garlands loosening; so for those who know your nature, is there any sorting of these as enemies and those as friends? Rider of the bird that took the thousand-headed serpent in its beak, first of time whom they call red-eyed Maal, we know your nature from the way they cry out to you.
nuance: The claim of line 58 is placed on the knower, not only on the god: it is those who know his nature (நின் மரபு அறிவோர்க்கே) who can no longer divide the world into his enemies and friends, though the same lines tell how the asuras fled from him in terror. Line 62 is hard to construe. Line 54 differs strongly from sangamtamil.com's text.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god as lord of gods and demons alike: paadaan

tamil: தீயினுள் தெறல் நீ; பூவினுள் நாற்றம் நீ;
கல்லினுள் மணியும் நீ; சொல்லினுள் வாய்மை நீ;
அறத்தினுள் அன்பு நீ; மறத்தினுள் மைந்து நீ;
வேதத்து மறை நீ; பூதத்து முதலும் நீ;
வெஞ் சுடர் ஒளியும் நீ; திங்களுள் அளியும் நீ;
அனைத்தும் நீ; அனைத்தின் உட்பொருளும் நீ; ஆதலின்,
பாழ் என, கால் என, பாகு என, ஒன்று என,
இரண்டு என, மூன்று என, நான்கு என, ஐந்து என,
ஆறு என, ஏழு என, எட்டு என, தொண்டு என,
reading: You are the burning in fire and the fragrance in the flower, the gem among stones and the truth in speech, the love in aram and the strength in valour, the secret of the Veda and the first of the elements, the light of the hot sun and the coolness of the moon; you are all things and the inner substance of all, so you have neither a dwelling nor a place to dwell; in the work of the first, middle and last orders there is no birth you have not taken and no one who gave you birth; with grace as your umbrella and aram as your sceptre you made the three-times-seven worlds a single shade with no second shade, and you are the one the count of the ages, void, quarter, half, one, two and on to nine, proclaims.
nuance: The 'X in Y' series (lines 63 to 68) names in each pair the quality that makes a thing what it is, so the god is the essence, not the bulk, of each; this is why the poet can conclude that he has no dwelling place. Lines 71 and 72 hold both that he is born in every order and that no one bore him. இரு நிழல் படாமை (line 75) borrows the king's boast of a single umbrella with no rival over the land. The numbers of line 77 (பாழ், கால், பாகு) may be zero, a quarter and a half, or void and categories of a cosmology; the reading is not fixed.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god as the essence of all and the sovereign of the worlds: paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the god's grace as the shelter of the worlds
the god's aram as the rule of the worlds

tamil: செங் கட் காரி! கருங் கண் வெள்ளை!
பொன் கட் பச்சை! பைங் கண் மாஅல்!
தொல் இயல் புலவ! நல் யாழ்ப் பாண!
reading: The poem closes in a litany of names: red-eyed dark one, black-eyed white one, gold-eyed green one, green-eyed Maal, cowherd and guardian, unseen ancient, unforgetting mind, unfailing king who rules the world, poet of the old way, bard of the fine lute, lord of the garland, of the undefeated horn, of the gold-twisted garment and the colour of the right-whorled conch, wielder of the wheel, wrestler of fighting strength, husband of Tiru; and it ends on the lotus cup that, in the first time before the great earth took shape, bloomed in the midst of the fearful flood together with the son of the true word, the shade of your wheel.
nuance: The names of lines 81 and 82 pair each eye with a body of another colour (red-eyed dark, black-eyed white, gold-eyed green, green-eyed Maal), giving the god several coloured forms at once, which echoes the difference of forms named in line 31. The last line ties the creation lotus that bore Brahma (line 93, cf. line 13) to the god's own wheel, but the syntax of line 94 is loose, and இடவல and குடஅல (line 83) are not clear.

thinai_evidence.note: the closing litany of the god's names: paadaan

title: திருமால் (4)
theme: Paripadal 4, to Tirumal: the praise that cannot add to his fame, his body like gem, sea and cloud, the Prahlada story of the embrace and the claws, his qualities parcelled out among the sun, moon, rain, earth, flower, water, sky and wind, all banners his and the snake-eating eagle decked with snakes, his harshness and grace answering what things hold, and his many places and names, ending with the god as the servant and refuge of each devotee.
source_issues: Paripadal 4: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; only the subject திருமால் is given, and the pan is பாலையாழ், a musical mode, not a thinai.
Paripadal 4 line 25 was flagged as a possible modern heading (heading_dropped), but it is the first of the eight parallel lines 25-32 (நின் வெம்மையும் விளக்கமும் ஞாயிற்று உள) and is verse; kept.

Paripadal 4 lines 8 and 20: lost vowel sign ொ restored in the -ஒடு fault (flags); lines 37 and 40 are not in sangamtamil.com (flag), though line 37 repeats line 36 as a linking refrain and line 40 fits the banner series.
Paripadal 4 line 65 (நின் ஓர் அன்ஓர் அந்தணர் அருமறை) looks corrupt at அன்ஓர், and lines 53-55 and 22-24 are hard to construe; readings there are tentative.

tamil: ஐந்து இருள் அற நீக்கி, நான்கினுள் துடைத்துத் தம்
ஒன்று ஆற்றுப்படுத்த நின் ஆர்வலர் தொழுது ஏத்தி,
நின் புகழ் விரித்தனர்; கிளக்குங்கால், அவை நினக்கு
நகுதலும் தகுதி, ஈங்கு ஊங்கு நிற் கிளப்ப;
வரு மழை இருஞ் சூல்-மூன்றும் புரையும் மா மெய்;
செயிர் தீர் செங் கட் செல்வ! நிற் புகழ
reading: Your devotees, having driven out the five darknesses and wiped clean within the four so that their one thing is guided to you, bow and spread your fame; we know well that our telling is no wonder to you, and that you may fairly laugh at our naming you here and there, yet we speak: your great body is like the sacred gem, the sea whose waves have stilled and the dark womb of the coming rain cloud, your garment is at odds with that dark body, your discus at odds with the lives of those who will not bear you, red-eyed lord without fault.
nuance: The counted words of lines 1 and 2 (ஐந்து இருள், நான்கினுள், தம் ஒன்று) are left unexplained by the poem; they read as a discipline of the worshipper (five things cleared away, four cleansed, one left to be guided to the god), not as part of the god's portrait. The double use of முரணிய (lines 8 and 9) sets the gold garment against the dark body and the discus against the god's foes in one figure of contrast.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god by his form and weapons: கடவுள் வாழ்த்து under paadaan (porul 2.27)

tamil: வலந்துழி, மலர்ந்த நோய் கூர் கூம்பிய நடுக்கத்து
நன்றா நட்ட அவன் நன் மார்பு முயங்கி,
தடி தடி பல பட-வகிர் வாய்த்த உகிரினை;
தாங்கி, இவ் உலகம் தந்து அடிப்படுத்ததை நடுவண்
reading: To praise you, the poet tells how Prahlada, heart smouldering and sandal paste dried, was bound and afflicted with many torments by his father, who scorned you while the son could not scorn you; you embraced the good chest of the one who loved you well and, with the drum roaring like thunder, burst from the broken pillar and with your claws tore again and again the mountain-like chest of the one who would not join you; and your bearing this world and bringing it under your feet is like the much-praised mountain that rises in the middle.
nuance: The poem sets the god's two acts on two chests side by side: நன்றா நட்ட அவன் நன் மார்பு முயங்கி (line 16) and ஒன்றா நட்டவன் உறு வரை மார்பின் (line 17); the same hands that embrace the son tear the father. The son is named பிருங்கலாதன் (line 12), a Tamil rendering of Prahlada, and the pillar appears only as ஒடி தூண் (line 20). Lines 22 to 24, on bearing the world, are hard to construe and may refer to another deed.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's deed against the devotee's father, sung as praise: paadaan

reading: Your heat and brightness are in the sun, your coolness and gentleness in the moon, your pouring and bounty in the rain, your sheltering and endurance in the earth, your fragrance and lustre in the flower, your appearance and breadth in water, your form and sound in the sky, your coming and withdrawing in the wind; so these things here, there and yonder, and all the rest, parted from you who are bound with protection, have come to their fitting places, lord of the high banner of the cock-bird.
nuance: The run of eight lines does not say the god is the sun or the moon; it says two of his qualities are found in each (நின் வெம்மையும் விளக்கமும் ஞாயிற்று உள), and line 34 says the things came about by parting from him (நிற் பிரிந்து). The world holds his qualities in pieces, each element two of them. The pairs are chosen to fit their element (sound to the sky, coming and withdrawing to the wind), which matches the order of qualities to elements later counted in the tattva lists.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's qualities found in the elements, sung as praise: paadaan

tamil: நின் ஒன்றா உயர் கொடி ஒன்று இன்று;
விடமுடை அரவின் உடல் உயிர் உருங்கு உவணம்;
பாம்பு படி மதம் சாய்த்தோய்! பசும் பூணவை
reading: Your high banner is the cock-bird; one high banner of yours is the palm, one the plough, one the elephant, and there is no high banner that is not yours; the eagle that crushes the body and life of the venomous snake wears snakes: a snake coiled on its lap, snakes for bangles, on its crown, as its ornament, on its head and on its wings; you who broke the pride of the snake, the one who sits on your banner with green ornaments has the snake for the prey he strikes.
nuance: The palm and the plough are the white elder god's marks (Paripadal 1 gives him the plough; Purananuru 56 gives him the palm banner), so the hymn takes the brother's banners as the dark god's own and then says no banner is not his (line 41). The snake passage turns on a paradox: the bird that devours snakes is adorned all over with them, the enemy worn as jewellery.

words: நின் ஒன்றா உயர் கொடி ஒன்று இன்று
thinai_evidence.note: the god's banners and his bird, sung as praise: paadaan

tamil: மனக்கோள் நினக்கு என வடிவு வேறு இலையே;
reading: Harm that afflicts and fierceness, and favour, cruelty and rightness, heat and coolness: where these are, you have them, and where they are not, you have none; you make no exchange between the lives of those who do not praise you and those who do; the saying that you have neither foes nor kin admits no exception, even when you gain those who praise you; you have no form other than the one the mind takes you to be.
nuance: Line 51 (உள்வழி உடையை; இல்வழி இலையே) makes the god's harshness and grace depend on where they are found, not on his preference, and line 56 makes his form the one the worshipper's mind holds (மனக்கோள் நினக்கு என வடிவு). The construal of lines 53 to 55 (மாற்று ஏமாற்றல்; அது போற்றுநர்ப் பெறினே) is doubtful: they may say instead that the god's impartiality yields to those who praise him.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's nature stated as praise: paadaan

tamil: கோள் இருள் இருக்கை ஆய் மணி மேனி,
நக்கு அலர் துழாஅய் நாறு இணர்க் கண்ணியை;
அழல் புரை குழை கொழு நிழல் தரும் பல சினை
கால் வழக்கு அறு நிலைக் குன்றமும், பிறவும்,
reading: Your body is a choice gem that holds the darkness, you wear a fragrant cluster-garland of opened tulasi, your chest bears the adorned mark that rose from gold; the lotus of ranked petals born from you, the measureless things of lotus-like eyes, your pair of feet that surpass you, the full gods that surpass you, and others besides: in the rare Veda of the brahmins, in the banyan of many branches with leaves like flame and rich shade, in the kadamba, in the middle of the good river, in the hill that stands where no foot goes and elsewhere, you dwell under a different name in each; you are the one in every place, the one who sits at peace in the folded hands of your devotees, the servant of each of them and the refuge of what each does.
nuance: Lines 62 and 63 say the god's feet and the full gods surpass the god himself (நின்னின் சிறந்த நின் தாள் இணையவை), so what is worshipped may be ranked above the one it belongs to. The closing lines go further: the god is the servant (ஏவலாளன்) of each worshipper. The sacred places of line 67 and 68 are the banyan, the kadamba, the river islet and the hill, each with its own name for the god.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's places and names, sung as praise: paadaan

title: செவ்வேள் (5)
theme: Paripadal 5, to Sevvel: the vel's deeds, the velan's rite placed within the god's bound, the birth from Siva's seed through the sacrificial fire and the six sages' wives, the gifts of the gods, and a prayer for grace, love and aram instead of wealth.
source_issues: Paripadal 5: the core text has 82 lines but the source numbers its last line 81 (printed 81 stands on line 82).
Paripadal 5 lines 12-14 are not in sangamtamil.com's text; line 78 differs strongly from theirs; ours kept (flags).
Paripadal 5 lines 5, 28 and 70: lost vowel sign ொ restored in the -ஒடு fault (flags).
Paripadal 5 line 31: விண்னோர் is a misprint for விண்ணோர்.
Paripadal 5: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; the pan is பாலையாழ், which is a musical mode, not a thinai.

tamil: பாய் இரும் பனிக் கடல் பார் துகள் படப் புக்கு,
சேய் உயர் பிணிமுகம் ஊர்ந்து, அமர் உழக்கி,
நோயுடை நுடங்கு சூர் மா முதல் தடிந்து,
கொன்று உணல் அஞ்சாக் கொடு வினைக் கொல் தகை
மாய அவுணர் மருங்கு அறத் தபுத்த வேல்,
நாவல்அம் தண் பொழில் வட பொழில் ஆயிடை,
குருகொடு பெயர் பெற்ற மால் வரை உடைத்து,
மூ-இரு கயந்தலை, முந் நான்கு முழவுத் தோள்,
ஞாயிற்று ஏர் நிறத் தகை! நளினத்துப் பிறவியை!
reading: The poet hails the spear that went into the wide cold sea until its floor was churned to dust, that rode the tall mount, cut down Sur at the root of his mango form and wiped out the deceiving asuras, and that split the great hill named after the crane; he names the god six-headed, twelve-shouldered, sun-coloured, born in the lotus, red Vel, son of the god of the kaaya tree, and then says that the praise and the possession rite the velan performs at festivals are neither true nor false, since this world has its limit in him and the high and low among all others are in his power.
nuance: Lines 16 and 17 are a small theology of the veri rite: the velan's cry is not dismissed as error (as the akam friend dismisses it) nor taken as plain truth; it is valid only because everything stands within the god's bound. Line 10 ends on மூ-இரு கயந்தலை and line 11 opens on the same words, a deliberate linking repetition. சிறப்போய் சிறப்பு இன்றிப் பெயர்குவை (line 18) can be read as 'you who are excellence go about without needing honour'; the sense is not secure. The hill split for its crane name is the one later poets call Krauncha.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god by his deeds and names: கடவுள் வாழ்த்து under paadaan (porul 2.27)

tamil: வேத மா பூண் வையத் தேர் ஊர்ந்து,
மூவகை ஆர் எயில் ஓர் அழல்-அம்பின் முளிய,
விரி கதிர் மணிப் பூணவற்குத் தான் ஈத்தது
எரி கனன்று ஆனாக் குடாரி கொண்டு அவன் உருவு
கருப் பெற்றுக் கொண்டோர், கழிந்த சேய் யாக்கை
நொசிப்பின், ஏழ் உறு முனிவர், நனி உணர்ந்து,
சாலார்; தானே தரிக்க என, அவர் அவி
உடன் பெய்தோரே, அழல் வேட்டு; அவ் அவித்
தடவு நிமிர் முத் தீப் பேணிய மன் எச்சில்,
வடவயின், விளங்கு ஆல், உறை எழு மகளிருள்
reading: The poet tells the birth: the green-eyed brahmin who ate the gods' share of the sacrifice, who with the first brahmin as charioteer, the Veda yoked to the earth for chariot, the serpent for bowstring and the mountain for bow, burned the three forts with one fiery arrow, joined Uma in a marriage whose union would not end; Indra won from the unwinking forehead eye a boon to stop it, and the truthful god, unwilling to take back his gift, split the embryo with a blazing axe; the seven sages, knowing, would not let their wives carry it and poured it as oblation into the fire, and of the seven women who live in the north six ate what remained of the three fires, all but Saalini, the one star, so that the great sages' wives of spotless chastity conceived you without failing in their chastity.
nuance: The story is built to keep chastity whole: the mothers conceive through the fire's leftover, not through a man, and the one wife who does not eat (Saalini, the star by the Seven) is singled out. Lines 36 to 41 are compressed and the exact order of the sages' decision (cut, refuse, pour into fire) is a reading, not a certainty.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's birth told as praise, under paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the bowstring of the archer of the three forts

tamil: நிவந்து ஓங்கு இமயத்து நீலப் பைஞ் சுனைப்
பெரும் பெயர் முருக! நிற் பயந்த ஞான்றே,
எரி உமிழ் வச்சிரம் கொண்டு, இகந்து வந்து, எறிந்தென,
அல்லல் இல் அனலன் தன் மெய்யின் பிரித்து,
வளம் கெழு செல்வன் தன் மெய்யின் பிரித்துத்
திகழ் பொறிப் பீலி அணி மயில் கொடுத்தோன்;
திருந்து கோல் ஞமன் தன் மெய்யின் பிரிவித்து,
இருங் கண் வெள் யாட்டு எழில் மறி கொடுத்தோன்;
ஆஅங்கு அவரும் பிறரும் அமர்ந்து படை அளித்த
வேறு வேறு உருவின் இவ் ஆறு இரு கைக் கொண்டு,
பொறி வரிக் கொட்டையொடு புகழ் வரம்பு இகந்தோய்
reading: They say the six bore you on a bed of lotus in the green pool of the towering Himalaya; on the day of your birth Indra came with his fire-spitting thunderbolt and struck, and you, cut into six, became six and were one; when in your play-war Indra was left empty-handed, Agni drew from his own body the cock, the rich lord of the sky the peacock with its spotted plumes, and Yama the ram, and with these and the weapons the others gave, bow, sword, spear, axe, pick, the sun, garland and bell, held in twelve hands, you passed beyond the fame of Indra himself.
nuance: அறு வேறு துணியும் அறுவர் ஆகி, ஒருவனை (lines 53, 54): Indra's blow, meant to destroy, is what makes him six and one; the gods' gifts come out of their own bodies (தன் மெய்யின் பிரித்து, three times), so the vahanas are presented as parts of the older gods given up to the younger. Lines 65 to 67 (மரனும், கனலியும்) and 70 (கொட்டை) are uncertain in what they name.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god's birth, victory and weapons, under paadaan

tamil: நின் குணம் எதிர்கொண்டோர் அறம் கொண்டோர் அல்லதை,
மன் குணம் உடையோர் மாதவர் வணங்கியோர் அல்லதை-
மறு பிறப்பு இல் எனும் மடவோரும், சேரார்
reading: Only those who take up your virtues and hold to aram, the good who bow to great ascetics, reach your shade; those whose hearts burn with lasting anger, those without aram, those whose penance has broken down and the fools who say there is no rebirth do not; so what we ask is not wealth, gold or pleasure but from you grace, love and aram, these three, you who wear the garland of round-clustered kadamba.
nuance: The prayer names what it refuses (பொருளும் பொன்னும் போகமும்) before what it asks, and the three it asks are ethical states, not gifts. Among those shut out are மறு பிறப்பு இல் எனும் மடவோர், the deniers of rebirth: a Sangam devotional poem already treats rebirth as a belief whose denial excludes one from the god.

thinai_evidence.note: a prayer to the god: paadaan

title: வையை (6)
theme: Paripadal 6, the Vaiyai in flood: rain fills the river, the town goes down to water-play, and a husband's quarrel with his wife over the women of the water is settled at the festival.
source_issues: Paripadal 6 line 14 is a modern prose heading left in the verse text (it summarises the bank breaking and the town rising); it is not verse.
Paripadal 6 line 68 is likewise a modern prose heading (it names the flood as the cause of the wilted shoots), not verse.
Paripadal 6: the core text has 107 lines but the source numbers its last line 106; printed line 15 stands on line 16 (flag), consistent with the heading at line 14 being counted.
Paripadal 6: the builder dropped lines it took for headings at positions 11, 48, 63 and 75 (flags); these could not be checked by eye against a second edition in the corpus.
Paripadal 6 line 63 is not in sangamtamil.com's text (flag); ours kept.
Paripadal 6: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; the pan is பாலையாழ், a musical mode, not a thinai.

tamil: நிறை கடல் முகந்து உராய், நிறைந்து, நீர் துளும்பும் தம்
நிலம் மறைவது போல் மலிர் புனல் தலைத் தலைஇ,
மலைய இனம் கலங்க, மலைய மயில் அகவ,
மலை மாசு கழியக் கதழும் அருவி இழியும்
மலி நீர் அதர் பல கெழுவு தாழ் வரை,
மாசு இல் பனுவற் புலவர் புகழ் புல
புகை, பூ, அவி ஆராதனை, அழல், பல ஏந்தி,
reading: The sky, having drawn water from the full sea, pours down to set its burden at rest; the flood rises as if to hide the land, the hill herds are troubled and the peacocks call, falls wash the mountain clean, and the cool water runs down the slopes and spreads fast and without pause, like the praise faultless poets keep weaving, so that the work of the fields thrives; and the Vaiyai's coming, met with incense, flowers, oblations and fire, is fit to bring smiling lovers together in their festival finery.
nuance: The song opens on the whole water cycle, sea to cloud to hill to river, and ends the sentence not on the harvest but on worship and on lovers dressed for the day (நாளணி): the river's use, for this poet, is the festival. The poets' unceasing verse is the river's measure, so the song names its own craft inside its first image.

thinai_evidence.note: the unit hails the river's arrival as a blessing, a praise poem under paadaan (porul 2.27)

comparisons.tenor: the swelling flood that spreads over the land

tamil: கொடி சேரா, திருக் கோவை காழ் கொளத்
தொகு கதிர் முத்துத் தொடை கலிழ்பு மழுக,
நகில் அணி அளறு நனி வண்டல் மண்ட,
திரைச் சிறை உடைத்தன்று கரைச்சிறை; அறைக எனும்
உரைச் சிறைப் பறை எழ, ஊர் ஒலித்தன்று
reading: As lovers of one desire, in an embrace that tightens bangles, shifts armlets, knots the girdle, muddies the pearl strings, smears the lac of nails and cheeks, turns breast paste to silt and mingles every ornament of breast and chest, break through the restraint that fills the heart, so the Vaiyai broke the dam of its hills; the drum of proclamation sounded, crying that the river's waves had broken the bank, and the whole town roared.
nuance: The simile runs the usual way backwards: seven lines of disordered ornaments come before we learn that the subject is a river; the reader first takes it for a love scene. நிறை (the heart's self-restraint) and சிறை (the dam) are set side by side, so the bank that breaks and the reserve that breaks are one word-play. Line 14 is not verse but a modern prose heading left in the text; it is marked here only because the unit must cover it.

thinai_evidence.note: the flood is pictured through lovers' embrace, the union of the river town

comparisons.tenor: the Vaiyai breaking its mountain-built dam

tamil: நீர் அணி அணியின் நிரைநிரை பிடி செல:
தணி புனல் ஆடும் தகை மிகு போர்க்கண்
துணி புனல் ஆக, துறை வேண்டும் மைந்தின்
நெய்ம் மாண் சிவிறியர், நீர் மணக் கோட்டினர்,
வெண் கிடை மிதவையர், நன் கிடைத் தேரினர்,
ஓர் இயவு உறுத்தர ஊர்ஊர்பு இடம் திரீஇச்
reading: On that day the cow elephants go down in rows, arrayed for water as the spotted-faced tusker is arrayed for war, and the young and the lovers, in fine dress and in wet dress, practise their rivalry in the play of the settling flood as if in battle: with garlands and gear they go down after the rushing current, on elephants' necks and spirited horses, with syringes and horns of scented water, on white pith floats and raft-chariots, the strong playing ford after ford and the well-off at the new water, until the river comes on smelling of juice, mud, ghee and flowers.
nuance: The festival is staged as a war (போர் அணி, இகல், அணி அணி ஆகிய தாரர்), with mounts, weapons and ranks, so the puram muster is borrowed for a love game. Lines 37 to 39 (சாரிகை மறுத்து ... சேரி இளையர்) are hard to construe and the reading of them is loose.

tamil: வேறுபடு புனல் என, விரை மண்ணுக் கலிழை,
வேறாகின்று இவ் விரி புனல் வரவு‘ என,
கரை அழி வால் அருவிக் கால் பாராட்ட,
புரைவது பூந் தாரான் குன்று‘ எனக் கூடார்க்கு
reading: Seeing the river come on reeking, the brahmins bent on their learning are dismayed, take it for a changed flood thick with fragrant clay, and cry that its goodness is gone, for flowers, garlands and wreaths, roots and stalks, fruits and tubers, the food of common people and spilled filtered toddy crowd its water; while the falls that break the hills are praised and the bank-breaking channels cheered, the flood goes down telling the unmated that the god's hill is like the rest between the breasts of lovers met by night, runs through the town, and at faint dawn the cool water of Tamil Vaiyai opens out on the land and shows plainly all that its water-army did in the dark.
nuance: The poet sets two judgments of one flood side by side without settling them: for the brahmins the festival water is defiled, for the town it is the season's joy, and the unit closes by calling it தமிழ் வையை, a river owned by the language. The night raid made visible at dawn is the lovers' night told as a river's: the flood's 'army' is the town's lovemaking. Lines 52 and 53 (வாதாலாட்ட, கால் பாராட்ட) are hard to fix, and the speakers of the two quoted cries are not named.

tamil: எய்தும் களவு இனி: நின் மார்பின் தார் வாடக்
கொய்ததும் வாயாளோ? கொய் தழை கை பற்றிச்
தளிரின் துவட்சிக்கு வையைப் பெருக்குக் காரணம் என
இன் இளவேனில், இது அன்றோ வையை? நின்
reading: The wife mocks her husband for the wilted shoots he brings, plucked for endless new guests, and asks whether the woman who wore them till his garland faded will not tell what he did with the leaf-skirt in his hand; he answers that the shoots drooped in the water and swears by the red god's hill that the Vaiyai's flood is to blame, and she agrees in scorn: does love keep one nature, now shrinking, now swelling, like the Vaiyai's flood in the rains and in early summer? Keep your Vaiyai, she says, under your own control.
nuance: The husband's alibi and the wife's retort use the same river: he blames the flood for the leaves, she turns the flood's rise and fall into the very proof of his changing love. நின் வையை வயமாக வை (line 79) is a gibe: 'your' Vaiyai, the excuse he keeps to hand. The speakers alternate without being named; lines 63 and 64 and 76 are obscure in our text, and line 68 is a modern prose heading, not verse.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife's quarrel with a husband she suspects of another woman, the marutham uri

tamil: செல் யாற்றுத் தீம் புனலில் செல் மரம் போல,
reading: The wife tells him that his chest, like a log drifting down the sweet flowing river, became a raft for women skilled at seizing, that he spent the night away, and that even now, like the spray that keeps welling after the breached sluice of the Vaiyai has been closed, he burns her: though he comes to put out her grief, his coming only keeps scorching the hearts of those whose eyes run with tears.
nuance: The images are taken from the day's own water-play: the floats and rafts of the festival become the husband, ridden by others. The dammed sluice that still seeps answers the reconciliation he expects: his return closes the breach, but the hurt goes on leaking. Line 82 (என்னும் பனியாய் இரவெல்லாம் வைகினை) is uncertain in its first words.

tamil: ‘நல்லாள் கரை நிற்ப, நான் குளித்த பைந் தடத்து,
நில்லாள் திரை மூழ்கி நீங்கி எழுந்து, என்மேல்
அல்லா விழுந்தாளை எய்தி, எழுந்து ஏற்று யான்
உள் அழுத்தியாள் எவளோ? தோய்ந்தது யாது?‘ என--
தேறித் தெரிய உணர் நீ: பிறிதும் ஓர்
‘இவ் வையை யாறு என்ற மாறு என்னை? கையால்
reading: The husband explains that while she stood on the bank a woman bathing in his pool, swept under by a wave, came up and fell on him unawares, and that before he could take hold of her she was up again; the wife asks who it was that pressed into his garland and what touched it, he tells her to understand that there is no other river but this Vaiyai to blame, and when she scorns the answer he swears with his hand on his head by cool Parankunram.
nuance: The festival gives the husband a ready alibi, since everyone is in the water together and bodies do collide; the poem lets the excuse be plausible and the suspicion be reasonable at once. The oath is by the god's hill above the river, the same Murugan shrine the Akananuru husbands swear by. Who speaks lines 92 to 96 is not marked in the text; the split given here is a reading.

tamil: துனி நீங்கி, ஆடல் தொடங்கு; துனி நனி
வல் இருள் நீயல்; அது பிழையாகும்‘ என,
reading: Others urge the wife: do not be angry; he fears the reddening of your eyes, so leave the sulk and begin the play, for a sulk that festers too long spoils love, and to burn and drive off into the dark night a heart that is yours alone would be the fault; and so, while the household plays and the skilled plead and labour until the sulk is understood, the lovers revel and bathe, grant grace and sulk again here and there as love puts out its tendrils, and the poet asks the Vaiyai that the love which has bloomed in the players' hearts may never fade.
nuance: The quarrel of the dialogue is not left to the two lovers: the town's skilled appeasers (வல்லவர்) do the work of reconciliation, and sulking is named as part of the play (அளிப்ப, துனிப்ப), not its interruption. The closing prayer turns the river from cause of the quarrel into keeper of the love. The counselors of lines 97 to 101 are not named; `pira` stands for them. The word கொடி for love's spreading is figurative, so it is not listed as karu.

title: வையை (7)
theme: Paripadal 7, to the Vaiyai: the rain-fed flood coming down from the hills to the Pandya fields, the town's cries and the river's spoils likened to the king's conquest, the lovers' quarrels of the water-play, and a closing prayer never to leave the river.
source_issues: Paripadal 7: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; only the subject வையை, the poet மையோடக் கோவனார், the music and the pan பாலையாழ் (a musical mode, not a thinai) are given.
Paripadal 7 line 85 has a gap (lacuna); the close of the prayer is incomplete.
Paripadal 7 lines 11 and 12 are not in sangamtamil.com's text; line 38 had ொ restored and line 81 was replaced by the sangamtamil.com reading (flags).
Paripadal 7 line 15: உய்ர்ந்துழி reads as a misprint for உயர்ந்துழி.
Paripadal 7 lines 36-37 and 54-57 are hard to construe: who is captured and who frees whom is not certain.

tamil: திரை இரும் பனிப் பௌவம் செவ்விதா அற முகந்து,
உர உரும் உடன்று ஆர்ப்ப, ஊர் பொறை கொள்ளாது,
கரை உடை குளமெனக் கழன்று, வான் வயிறு அழிபு,
இரவு இருள் பகலாக, இடம் அரிது செலவு என்னாது,
நிலன் உற நிமிர் தானை நெடு நிரை நிவப்பு அன்ன--
பெயலான் பொலிந்து, பெரும் புனல் பல நந்த,
நலன் நந்த நாடு அணி நந்தப் புலன் நந்த
ஒளிர் சினை வேங்கை விரிந்த இணர் உதிரலொடு,
வளி வாங்கு சினைய மா மரம் வேர் கீண்டு,
உழவர் களி தூங்க, முழவு பணை முரல,
வேண்டு வழி நடந்து, தாங்கு தடை பொருது;
விதி ஆற்றான் ஆக்கிய மெய்க் கலவை போலப்
பொது நாற்றம் உள்உள் கரந்து, புது நாற்றம்
reading: Clouds that have drawn up the cold dark sea break open like a tank whose bank has given way, with thunder roaring, and white falls wind round every hill like the risen ranks of the Pandya's army marching day and night on its chosen land; so the Vaiyai's water comes, swelling the land's good and its beauty, scattering narantham and vengai flowers, uprooting wind-bent trees and spreading their fruit over the low ground; while the ploughmen revel and the drums sound, it goes where it will like a girl who knows no dance and a joyful one who knows no sulking, fighting every dam, and like a paste mixed by rule it hides the common smells within and gives off a new fragrance, this red-flowered flood.
nuance: The flood is carried by the cycle that begins at sea (line 1) and ends in the fields' good (line 9, நலன் நந்த நாடு அணி நந்த), so the praise of the river is also praise of rain. The two similes of lines 17 and 18 already give the river a woman's temper, a girl untaught and without oodal, which the water-play later in the song turns round: there the women quarrel and the river stays calm.
