tamil: முகிழ் மயங்கு முல்லை முறை நிகழ்வு காட்ட,
மணி மருள் நல் நீர்ச் சினை மடமயில் அகவ,
வௌவல் கார் இருள் மயங்கு மணி மேனியன்,
reading: The monkey with her young clasped to her leaps from rock to rock, the budding mullai shows the seasons turning in order, the young peahen calls from branches over water clear as gems, leaves fall and the koels call, flute and cymbals play and the singers' practised songs answer the drum, so that the hill's echo never stops: to this dark hill of him who overcame and slew his foes go, with your wives, with your parents, with the infants in your arms and with those you love, honouring the god and bowing toward his quarter; he is the one with eyes like the lotus, his gem-like body mingled with the dark of the rainy night, who appears in whatever world it may be and takes away the suffering when its people are troubled, and who dwells in love on Irunkunram.
nuance: The call to pilgrimage names the whole household one by one (wives, parents, infants, loved ones), so the worship is a family journey, not a lone ascetic's. The god's coming is stated in general (எவ்வயின் உலகத்தும் தோன்றி) and his dwelling in particular (இருங்குன்றத்தான்), and the hinge between them is love (அன்பு-அது மேஎய்).

thinai_evidence.note: a call to go and worship the god who removes suffering: paadaan

tamil: கள் அணி பசுந் துளவினவை, கருங் குன்றனையவை;
புகர் இணர் சூழ் வட்டத்தவை; புகர் வாளவை;
நலம் புரீஇ அம் சீர் நாம வாய்மொழி
இது என உரைத்தலின், எம் உள் அமர்ந்து இசைத்து, இறை,
reading: He is named by what he bears: the honeyed fresh tulasi and a form like a dark hill, the bright light and the single earring, the bird on the golden banner, the plough with its strong ring, the club held in anger, the right-whorled conch and the strong discus, the striped bow and its arrows, the disc ringed with bright clusters and the bright sword; since the true sacred word says this is so, and the lord dwells within us and sounds there, we bow and praise the two of great name, asking that we may come to dwell at the feet on Irunkunram.
nuance: The litany runs in plurals (-அவை) and mixes the marks of both brothers, the elder's single earring and plough with the younger's tulasi, conch and discus, so the weapons are counted as one possession; only the last line says the praise goes to two (பெரும் பெயர் இருவரை). The god is placed at once on the hill and inside the worshipper (எம் உள் அமர்ந்து இசைத்து), and the prayer asks for the hill.

thinai_evidence.note: closing praise and prayer to the two gods: paadaan

tamil: கரையே--கை வண் தோன்றல் ஈகை போன்ம் என,
துறையே--முத்து நேர்பு புணர் காழ், மத்தக நித்திலம்,
பொலம் புனை அவிர் இழை, கலங்கல் அம் புனல் மணி
வலம் சுழி உந்திய, திணை பிரி புதல்வர்
செறுவே--விடு மலர் சுமந்து, பூ நீர் நிறைதலின்,
படு கண் இமிழ் கொளை பயின்றனர் ஆடும்,
களி நாள் அரங்கின் அணி நலம் புரையும்.
கரைபு ஒழுகு தீம் புனற்கு எதிர் விருந்து அயர்வ போல்.
தேன் உண்டு பாடத் திசைதிசைப் பூ நலம்
reading: The banks, as if copying the giving of a generous-handed lord, wear away everywhere under the pepper and sandal of the dark hill, the foam of curd and much else; at the fords women with darting eyes come crowd after crowd to bathe with their partners, holding their little tufted sons with the munjam on their heads, while pearl strings, pearls from the elephant's brow, gold jewels and gems whirl to the right in the turbid water; the fields, carrying shed flowers and brimming with flower-water, are as lovely as a stage on festival day where dancers trained to the drum's beat perform; the groves give their fragrant narantham, thick with the pollen the bees hum over, as if feasting the sweet flowing water as a guest; in forest groves, ponds and islets the bees drink and sing, and flower-beauty bloomed in every quarter: such is the Vaiyai's coming.
nuance: The unit is built on four places, each with its own simile: banks (கரையே), fords (துறையே), fields (செறுவே), groves (காவே). The banks' loss to the flood is praised as giving, and the groves' flowers as a host's welcome, so the river is both the guest that is fed and the cause of a generosity that costs the land.

thinai_evidence.note: the river's coming praised, the frame of the song: paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the banks giving up their goods to the flood
the groves giving flowers to the flood

tamil: குரும்பையின் முலைப் பட்ட பூ நீர் துடையாள்,
பூத்தனள்; நீங்கு‘ எனப் பொய் ஆற்றால், தோழியர்--
தோற்றம் ஓர் ஒத்த மலர் கமழ் தண் சாந்தின்
இருங் கடற்கு ஊங்கு இவரும் யாறு எனத் தங்கான்,
மகிழ, களிப் பட்ட தேன் தேறல் மாற்றி,
reading: Her companions splash water all round, and a girl who has not wiped the flower-water from her young breasts sees a noble young man coming and presses her thick cloth's hem to herself, while her friends tell him by a lie, 'don't come near, she is in her flowering, go'; they guard her with the scent of cool sandal that looks just like blood and send him off laughing; but he, like a river rushing on to the great sea, does not hold back, leaves the heady honeyed wine, comes close without wiping away the red, and embraces her sweetly, so that their cry 'the lady has flowered, hail!' turned to shame: such is the Vaiyai's coming.
nuance: The friends use the bar of menstruation (பூத்தனள்) to keep a lover off, with red sandal standing in for blood; he ignores the bar, and the same word comes back as a joke (பூத்தனள் நங்கை; பொலிக). Whose shame line 30 means, the girl's or the lying friends', is not fixed by the text. The refrain வையை வரவு makes the scene part of the flood's arrival.

thinai_evidence.note: the lover breaks through a feigned bar to embrace the girl at the river

comparisons.tenor: the young man pressing on undeterred

tamil: மலையின் இழி அருவி மல்கு இணர்ச் சார்ச் சார்க்
நனை சேர் கதுப்பினுள் தண் போது, மைந்தர்
மலர் மார்பின் சோர்ந்த மலர் இதழ், தா அய்;
மீன் ஆரம் பூத்த வியன் கங்கை நந்திய
reading: The falls coming down from the hill join the bank trees beside the groves full of clusters and grow lovely, and the cool buds from the women's hair and the petals slipped from the men's flowered chests spread over the water, so that the Vaiyai, humming with bees, always looks like the sky where the wide Ganga of the heavens, flowered with stars, has passed.
nuance: The stars are said to flower (மீன் ஆரம் பூத்த), so the simile runs both ways: flowers on the river are stars, and the stars of the heavenly river are flowers. The flowers are the lovers' castoffs, so the river's sky is made of the night's adornments.

thinai_evidence.note: the river's constant beauty praised: paadaan

comparisons.vehicle: மீன் ஆரம் பூத்த வியன் கங்கை நந்திய வானம்
comparisons.tenor: the river strewn with fallen flowers

tamil: ஒள் ஒளி சேய்தா ஒளி கிளர் உண் கண் கெண்டை,
பல் வரி வண்டினம் வாய் சூழ் கவினொடும்,
வெல் நீர் வீவயின் தேன் சோர, பல் நீர்
வடுப் படு மான்மதச் சாந்து ஆர் அகலத்தான்,
எடுத்த வேய் எக்கி நூக்கு உயர்பு தாக்கத்
தொடுத்த தேன் சோரும் வரை போலும், தோற்றம்--
reading: In toddy, in water and in sulking, these three, the women's bright kohl-lined eyes, red-streaked like kendai fish, with bee swarms circling their mouths and honey dripping where the flowers fall, the bathers who plunge again and again in the deep water are embraced, and the man whose chest is smeared with musk paste and marked with scars yields to them; the sight is like a hill where a hanging honeycomb drips when bent bamboo springs up and strikes it: such is the nature of the Vaiyai of the king of the bannered chariot.
nuance: The three in which the eyes redden, toddy, water and the sulk, set drink, bathing and quarrel side by side as one play. The closing simile makes the embrace a sudden release, as the bamboo springs back and the honey falls. The syntax of lines 40 to 44 is loose, and who embraces whom can be read more than one way.

thinai_evidence.note: lovers embrace at the river after drink and sulking

tamil: நாள் நாள், உறையும், நறுஞ் சாந்தும், கோதையும்,
reading: Clouds roar on the hills and this sweet water roars in waves on the banks; so that those who wear chaplets, chest garlands and fragrant hair garlands may take by bathing, day after day, the fruit of the gifts they have made, may the sky never refuse to keep the rain, the fragrant sandal, the garlands, the flowering smoke and the offerings from drying, and may your flood swell and never run dry, Vaigai.
nuance: The prayer ties rite to rain: the sky is asked not to let the offerings dry (புலராமை), and bathing in the river is when the giver collects the fruit of past giving (பண்ணிய ஈகைப் பயன்). The river is addressed directly only in the last word, நினக்கு.

thinai_evidence.note: closing prayer to sky and river: paadaan

title: செவ்வேள் (17, 18)
theme: Paripadal 17 and 18, to Murugan of Parankunram: worship on the hill where every festival sound meets a rival sound of nature, the crowded road from Koodal, the hill rivalling the god's other hill, lovers' sulks mended and a bard's lies refuted on it, and prayers to dwell at the god's feet with kin.
source_issues: Paripadal 17 and 18: the colophons have no thinai or thurai; only the subject செவ்வேள், the poets, the music and the pans நோதிறம் and காந்தாரம் (musical modes, not thinais) are given.

Paripadal 17 line 4: பரவினர் உரையொடு had its vowel sign ொ restored by rule (flag); not confirmed by sangamtamil.com. A line before line 9 was dropped as a modern heading (flag); the run of ஒருதிறம் clauses reads as complete.

Paripadal 18 line 7, தலைமகன் ஊடல் உணர்ப்பிக்கும் திறம், reads as a prose heading, not verse; it would account for the text having 57 lines where the source numbers its last line 56. It is kept in the unit so the line numbers stay those `show` prints.
Paripadal 18 line 10 was repaired from sangamtamil.com, and the printed line number 10 stands on line 11 (flags); a line before line 16 was dropped as a modern heading (flag).

Paripadal 18 line 18: வடு வொடு is printed as two words; read as வடுவொடு. Line 27: விரை மயில் வேல் ஞாயிறு and lines 31-32 and 42-46 (the quiver image and the address to one skilled at dice) are hard to construe.
Paripadal 17 line 46: கை ஊழ் தடுமாற்றம் is obscure; read here as the festival and feasting passing in turn between hill, river and city.

tamil: தேம் படு மலர், குழை, பூந் துகில், வடி மணி,
கோல் எரி, கொளை, நறை, புகை, கொடி, ஒருங்கு எழ--
ஒருதிறம், பாணர் யாழின் தீங் குரல் எழ,
ஒருதிறம், யாணர் வண்டின் இமிர் இசை எழ,
ஒருதிறம், கண் ஆர் குழலின் கரைபு எழ,
ஒருதிறம், பண் ஆர் தும்பி பரந்து இசை ஊத,
ஒருதிறம், மண் ஆர் முழவின் இசை எழ,
ஒருதிறம், அண்ணல் நெடு வரை அருவி நீர் ததும்ப,
ஒருதிறம், பாடல் நல் விறலியர் ஒல்குபு நுடங்க,
ஒருதிறம், வாடை உளர்வயின் பூங் கொடி நுடங்க,
ஒருதிறம், பாடினி முரலும் பாலை அம் குரலின்
ஒருதிறம், ஆடு சீர் மஞ்ஞை அரி குரல் தோன்ற,
மாறுமாறு உற்றன் போல் மாறு எதிர் கோடல்
reading: Carrying honeyed flowers, tender leaves, flowered cloth, cast bells and the raised leaf-spear, mixing sandal, the velan ties a ram at the guarded tree and the worshippers praise with words and with tuned song; on this hill whose trees are wet with the honey of open flowers, torch, song, fragrance, smoke and banners rise together, and those who join the god's feet evening after evening want no dwelling of the gods above; on one side the bards' lute sounds and on another the bees hum, here the flute and there the tumbi drones its tune, here the drum and there the waterfall brims, here the singing women sway and there the flower creepers sway in the north wind, here the paadini's paalai voice shows the rising and falling notes and there the peacock calls, so that, as if in rivalry, each answers the other: such is the hill of him who slew the foe.
nuance: The passage is built as ten alternating sides (ஒருதிறம்), and each human performance is matched by a thing of the hill doing the same act: lute and bee, flute and tumbi, drum and falls, swaying singers and swaying creepers, the paadini's voice and the peacock's. The closing line names the god by the same word as the contest, மாறு: the slayer of the foe (மாறு அட்டான்) owns a hill where every sound meets its rival (மாறு எதிர் கோடல்). Line 8 sets the worship above heaven itself: who would want the gods' abode?

thinai_evidence.note: worship and praise of the god's hill: கடவுள் வாழ்த்து under paadaan

comparisons.vehicle: மாறுமாறு உற்றன் போல் மாறு எதிர் கோடல்
comparisons.tenor: the festival's music and the hill's own sounds answering one another side by side

tamil: மகிழ் மிகு தேஎம் கோதையர் கூந்தல் குஞ்சியின்
சோர்ந்து அவிழ் இதழின் இயங்கும் ஆறு இன்று.
ஆவி உண்ணும் அகில் கெழு கமழ் புகை
வாய்வாய் மீ போய், உம்பர் இமைபு இறப்ப;
மனம் மகிழ் தூங்குநர் பாய்பு உடன் ஆட,
சுனை மலர்த் தாது ஊதும் வண்டு ஊதல் எய்தா;
reading: On the road between Koodal, rich in song and fame, and Parankunram, people revel smeared with fragrant sandal, so crowded that what is near and near again is far and far, and petals loosened from the women's garlands and the men's tufts leave no room to walk; on the hill that sends its fragrance to every quarter by blameless truth and sacrifice, the smoke of agil that consumes the offerings rises here and there till the gods above blink and the unwaning sun cannot be seen; and women with bangled forearms and soft shoulders, men with garlanded chests, all leap together on the swings, so that the bees that suck the pollen of the pool flowers cannot get to them: such is the beauty of Parankunram.
nuance: Each image measures the crowd by what it blocks: the near road becomes far, the fallen petals close the path, the smoke shuts out the sun and makes even the unblinking gods blink (இமைபு), and the swingers keep the bees from the pool flowers. The festival is praised by its excess, not by any rite described in detail.

thinai_evidence.note: the festival beauty of the god's hill described as praise: paadaan

tamil: கீழோர் வயல் பரக்கும், வார் வெள் அருவி பரந்து ஆனாது ஆரோ;
மேலோர் இயங்குதலால், வீழ் மணி நீலம் செறு உழக்கும் அரோ;
அவ் வெள் அருவி அணி பரங் குன்றிற்கும்,
தொய்யா விழுச் சீர் வளம் கெழு வையைக்கும்,
கொய் உளை மான் தேர்க் கொடித்தேரான் கூடற்கும்,
மணி நிற மஞ்ஞை ஓங்கிய புட் கொடி,
reading: The long white falls spread over the fields of those below without ceasing, and as those above move about, the gems they drop churn the blue paddy plots; the god's festival and the fine feasting of guests pass, hand to hand in turn, between this hill of white falls, the Vaiyai of unfailing wealth and the Koodal of the king of the maned-horse banner chariot, and that alternation is good; so the poet turns to the god, lord who rode Pinimukam, with the peacock raised on his bird banner, and says: leaving other service and praising your fame, we sing your tall hill and bow, we and our kin, that we may have days of safety.
nuance: The hill, the river and the city are joined by one exchange: the falls water the fields below, and the god's festival and the feasting of guests move between the three places. பிணிமுகம் is the name of the god's mount; whether it is the elephant or the peacock is not settled from this line, which also names the peacock on the banner.

thinai_evidence.note: description of the hill's bounty ending in the closing prayer of the hymn: paadaan

tamil: போர் எதிர்ந்து ஏற்றார் மதுகை மதம் தப,
கார் எதிர்ந்து ஏற்ற கமஞ் சூல் எழிலிபோல்,
நீர் நிரந்து ஏற்ற நிலம் தாங்கு அழுவத்து,
சூர், நிரந்து சுற்றிய, மா தபுத்த வேலோய்! நின்
சீர் நிரந்து ஏந்திய குன்றொடு நேர் நிரந்து,
reading: O spear-bearer who, like the full-bellied cloud that meets the rainy season, met those who came against you in battle and broke the pride of their strength, and who in the water-spread expanse that holds up the earth destroyed the mango of Sur and his ring of attendants: this hill takes up the challenge of standing level with the hill that bears your glory.
nuance: The hill is not said to equal the god's other hill outright: ஏறுமாறு ஏற்கும் makes it a contender that accepts the contest, the same language of rivalry the companion song 17 uses for the hill's sounds.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's victory over Sur sung as praise: paadaan

comparisons.vehicle: கார் எதிர்ந்து ஏற்ற கமஞ் சூல் எழிலிபோல்
comparisons.tenor: the god meeting his foes in battle

tamil: ஒள் ஒளி மணிப் பொறி ஆல் மஞ்ஞை நோக்கித் தன்
‘உள்ளியது உணர்ந்தேன்; அஃது உரை இனி, நீ எம்மை
எள்ளுதல் மறைத்தல் ஓம்பு‘ என்பாளைப் பெயர்த்து, அவன்,
‘காதலாய்! நின் இயல் களவு எண்ணிக் களி மகிழ்
பேதுற்ற இதலைக் கண்டு, யான் நோக்க, நீ எம்மை
reading: Seeing her man gaze at a bright peacock with gem-like eyespots and brood within, the woman of the lovely brow says she knows what he was thinking and bids him tell it and not mock her or hide it; he answers: my love, I was thinking how the peacock had stolen your bearing, and when I looked at a quail dazed in its revelry you looked at me as at a stranger; so he talks her out of the sulk, and that, says the poet, is the way of the god's hill.
nuance: The quarrel turns on a look: she reads his silent gaze as thought of another woman, he turns the same gaze into praise of her, because what he was looking at had taken her nature (நின் இயல் களவு). The scene is offered as the hill's character (குன்ற இயல்பு), so the god's hill is praised by the quick mending of lovers' quarrels on it. Why the quail enters his answer is not clear.

thinai_evidence.note: a sulk at the husband's gaze, talked away: marutham's uri set on the kurinji hill

comparisons.vehicle: ஒள் ஒளி மணிப் பொறி ஆல் மஞ்ஞை
comparisons.tenor: the woman's bearing, which the peacock has stolen

tamil: ஐ வளம் பூத்த அணி திகழ் குன்றின்மேல்,
மை வளம் பூத்த மலர் ஏர் மழைக் கண்ணார்,
கை வளம் பூத்த வடு வொடு, காணாய் நீ?
மொய் வளம் பூத்த முயக்கம், யாம் கைப்படுத்தேம்:
மெய் வளம் பூத்த விழை தகு பொன் அணி--
நை வளம் பூத்த நரம்பு இயை சீர்ப் பொய் வளம்
reading: On the lovely hill where every kind of richness blooms, she says to the bard: do you not see the marks that the hands of women with rain-cool eyes like collyrium-dark flowers have made bloom on him? we have caught the embrace that bloomed thick, and the desirable gold ornaments that bloomed on his body; bard, your song on tuned strings has bloomed only a richness of lies.
nuance: Every line turns on the same phrase, வளம் பூத்த, so the hill's blooming richness, the marks on the man, the embrace and the ornaments all bloom alike, and the bard's song blooms too, but with lies. The speaker is not named; the wife is the likeliest reading of யாம் கைப்படுத்தேம், though the friend speaking for her is possible.

thinai_evidence.note: the bard's message refused because the marks of other women are seen: the marutham sulk

tamil: தண் தளிர் தருப் படுத்து, எடுத்து உரைஇ,
வெண் சுடர் வேல் வேள்! விரை மயில் வேல் ஞாயிறு!--நின்
ஒண் சுடர் ஓடைக் களிறு ஏய்க்கும் நின் குன்றத்து,
reading: O Vel of the white-flaming spear, sun of the swift peacock and the spear: on your hill, which with its victorious peaks where the rain clouds thundered over gathered tender shoots, and with its creeper lightning that dazzles the eyes, flares, presses on and splits the dark, looks like your elephant with its bright forehead plate, stands the city where the lovely painted hall is the seat of the work of Kama's arrows.
nuance: The hill is first likened to the god's own war elephant, the lightning playing the part of its gleaming forehead plate, and then holds a painted hall given over to the god of love's arrows: the war god's hill houses the love god's work.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god and his hill: paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the god's hill with its lightning

tamil: ஆர் ததும்பும் அயில் அம்பு நிறை நாழி
போர் தோற்றுக் கட்டுண்டார் கை போல்வ--கார் தோற்றும்
கவின் முகை, கட்டு அவிழ்ப்ப, தும்பி; கட்டு யாழின்
வில்லுச் சொரி பகழியின், மென் மலர் தாயின
reading: With groves on the dread-haunted slopes thick as a quiver full of sharp arrows, the pools brim with rain water and the clustered flowers brim with beauty; the close-packed kanthal that heralds the rains is like the hands of men defeated in war and bound, and the tumbi bees loosening the bound buds are like hands loosening the twisted strings of a lute; the wind of the dewy season has drawn on the lovely clouds the rainbow of the thunderbolt-bearer, and on the mountain, you who are skilled at the game of dice, the trees have spread soft flowers like arrows rained from a bow.
nuance: Two linked images use one bud: the closed kanthal is a bound captive's hands, and the bee that opens it is a player's hand loosening lute strings, so the flower passes from an image of war to one of music. The address வல்லுப் போர் வல்லாய், to one skilled in dice, begins the dice imagery of the next lines; who is addressed is not clear.

thinai_evidence.note: description of the god's hill in the rains, within praise: paadaan

the soft flowers the trees spread

tamil: வானில் அணித்த, வரி ஊதும் பல் மலரால்,

reading: You skilled at rolling dice: on the mountain, with the swelling clatter of the long throw, like the din of battle, the clouds roar and stand; as the falls roar the peaks wear pearls, as the sparrows chirp the millet bends its ears, the kites gather, and the pools, with many flowers where striped bees hum, curve like the lovely rainbow set in the sky; and where strings and song join, where the sruti, flowers and lamps come together and burning agil and sandal give their fragrance, lord of the army with the war spear, may we stay at your feet without parting, with our kin, as one comes to dwell in the town that is rightly one's own.
nuance: The closing prayer asks not for gifts but for dwelling: to stay at the god's feet as in one's own rightful town, never parting (பிரியாது), the same word akam uses for lovers. The run of lines 46 to 51 pairs each sound of the hill with what it brings about (falls and pearls, sparrows and millet); எருவை may be the kite or a kind of reed, and lines 43 to 46 are hard to construe.

thinai_evidence.note: the closing prayer of the hymn: paadaan

title: செவ்வேள் (19)
theme: Paripadal 19, to Sevvel at Parankunram: the hill as heaven's gift to earth and its rival weddings, the pilgrims' road from Koodal, the Pandya king circling the hill, the painted hall with its explainers, the lost girl and the echo, the flowering slopes, the maidens' rite of the elephant's leftover, and the closing praise of the red god.
source_issues: Paripadal 19: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; only the subject செவ்வேள், the poet நப்பண்ணனார், the music by மருத்துவன் நல்லச்சுதனார் and the pan காந்தாரம் (a musical mode, not a thinai).
Paripadal 19 lines 9, 39 and 68 are not in sangamtamil.com's text; ours kept (flags). Lines 8, 20, 32, 41 and 89 are flagged as near a dropped modern heading; check by eye.
Paripadal 19 line 6: -ளொடு restored by rule in துறக்கத்தவளொடு, not confirmed by sangamtamil.com (flag).
Paripadal 19 line 43: வேள்லியின் reads as a misprint for வேள்வியின்.
Paripadal 19 line 85: நின யானைச் reads as a misprint for நின் யானைச்; குங்குமத் தால் is split for குங்குமத்தால்.

Paripadal 19 lines 24-25 (பழ மதிச் சூடி அசையும் சுவல்மிசைத் தானையின்), 30 (தும்பி twice, bee or elephant), 40 (தெய்வப் பிரமம்) and 67-73 (பல்லவன் and the girls' words) are hard to construe; the readings given are provisional.

tamil: நில வரை அழுவத்தான் வான் உறை புகல் தந்து,
புல வரை அறியாத புகழ் பூத்த கடம்பு அமர்ந்து,
இரு நிலத்தோரும் இயைக!‘ என, ஈத்த நின்
தண் பரங்குன்றத்து, இயல் அணி, நின் மருங்கு
அறம் பெரிது ஆற்றி, அதன் பயன் கொண்மார்,
உரி மாண் புனை கலம் ஒண் துகில் தாங்கி,
புரி மாண் புரவியர், போக்கு அமை தேரர்,
தெரி மலர்த் தாரர், தெரு இருள் சீப்ப, நின்
நேர் பூ நிறை பெய்து இரு நிலம் பூட்டிய
தார் போலும், மாலைத் தலை நிறையால்--தண் மணல்
reading: The poet says that at cool Parankunram, which the god seated by the famed kadambu gave so that the people of the wide earth too might share what the worthy of the sages' line enjoy, the adorned wedding with the peacock-like bride beside him seems to vie with that of the bride from heaven; and that at the end of night the crowds of Koodal, never beaten in learning or in war, go out in fine ornaments and bright cloth, on horses and in chariots, wearing chosen garlands and driving the dark from the streets, like doers of great aram setting out for the world of the excellent to take its fruit, so that the whole way from the hill to Koodal, packed with garlanded heads, is like a garland laid on the earth: the cool-sanded road the pilgrims take.
nuance: The hill is framed as a gift: heaven's enjoyment brought within reach of ordinary people (lines 1 to 5). The peacock-creeper bride (மயிற்கொடி) is most likely Valli and the one of heaven (துறக்கத்தவள்) the daughter of Indra, so the earthly wedding is said to rival the heavenly one; the construal of lines 5 to 7 is not secure. The festival crowd is pictured through the reward of aram, riders in finery going to heaven, which turns a pilgrimage into a foretaste of the world to come.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god's hill and of the pilgrimage to it, under paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the bride of the earthly wedding
the festival crowds setting out from Koodal
the unbroken line of garlanded heads on the road from the hill to Koodal

tamil: சூர் உறை குன்றின் தட வரை ஏறி மேல்
பாடு வலம் திரி பண்பின்-- பழ மதிச்
படு மணி யானை நெடியாய்! நீ மேய
தும்பி தொடர் கதுப்ப தும்பி தொடர் ஆட்டி,
வம்பு அணி பூங் கயிறு வாங்கி, மரன் அசைப்பார்--
வண் தார்ப் புரவி வழி நீங்க வாங்குவார்;
குருகு எறி வேலோய்! நின் குன்றக் கீழ் நின்ற
reading: Like the stars that circle Meru with the sun, the Pandya Vazhuthi of the excellent land, with the women of his household gentle as young peahens and his officers who know their duty, climbs the broad slope of the god's hill where the fearful powers dwell and goes round it to the right, and the whole land and city arrive with cloths swaying on shoulders, singing tongues and spreading joy; and when one tells of the guarded town around the tall lord of the belled elephant, the ground below the hill, where people tie elephants to trees with flowered ropes, lead garlanded horses off the road, halt strong chariots along the way and feed mouthfuls of sugarcane, is like the camp of a king whose army has rearing horses: that is how we praise it.
nuance: The king does not go before the god as a ruler receiving homage: he joins the circling crowd, and the poet likens his round to the stars that go round Meru with the sun, so the shrine becomes the centre and the Pandya one of its orbiting lights. The pilgrims' camp below the hill is in turn likened to a war camp, the king's world borrowed to describe a festival.

thinai_evidence.note: the king's procession round the god's hill, told as praise of the god

comparisons.tenor: the king and his train going round the hill
the women of the king's household
the crowded ground below the hill

tamil: என்றூழ் உற வரும் இரு சுடர் நேமி
சென்ற கவுதமன்; சினன் உறக் கல் உரு
ஒன்றிய படி இது‘ என்று உரை செய்வோரும்:
நேர் வரை விரி அறை வியல் இடத்து இழைக்கச்
reading: Beside the temple of Maal Murugan on clear Parankunram stands a hall of paintings in its beauty: around it some give food to the monkeys and sugarcane to the black-faced langurs, some play the divine pirama, some set fingers to the flute, some tune the ili and kural strings of the lute, some speak of the beauty of the sacrifice, some beat the drum in order while the taut string hums, and some lose themselves in the picture of the wheel of the two lights that summer brings; some answer the curious who ask who is who, saying 'this is Rati and this Kama', and some explain 'this is Indra as a cat, she is Ahalya, he is Gautama who had gone out, and this is how she took the form of stone in his anger': many such paintings, drawn across the wide rooms of the facing rock, so that visitors point and are taught by pointing.
nuance: This is one of the earliest Tamil records of a painted shrine hall and of how it was used: not only looked at but explained aloud, story by story, to visitors who asked (வினவ, வினா இறுப்போரும்; சுட்டவும், சுட்டு அறிவுறுத்தவும்). The paintings are of northern stories (Rati and Kama, Indra, Ahalya and Gautama) beside a Tamil god's temple. தெய்வப் பிரமம் (line 40) is read as a stringed instrument, and what the sun-and-moon picture shows (lines 46, 47) is not certain.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's temple and its painted hall described as praise

tamil: அவ் இசை முழை ஏற்று அழைப்ப, அழைத்துழிச்
reading: A simple girl strays from the kin she came with, wanders in among the rocks and, lost, cries that she has forgotten even the path she came by, calling 'ee! oo!' to her people; the call that they do not take up is taken up by the echoing cave, which calls back, and she goes where it called, finds no kin there, turns back and calls 'koo, koo' once more: such, full of innocence, is the hill of the god who delights in praise.
nuance: The innocence (மடமைத்தே) is given to the hill itself: the cave answers a call it does not understand, as artless as the girl who follows its answer, so the joke falls on the hill as much as on her. ஏலா அவ் விளி (line 62) is the call her kin do not answer.

thinai_evidence.note: a scene on the god's hill told as part of his praise

tamil: நனி நுனி நயவரு சாய்ப்பின் நாறு இணர்ச்
சினை போழ் பல்லவன் தீம் சுனை உதிர்ப்ப,
ஐந் தலை அவிர் பொறி அரவம்; மூத்த
மைந்தன்; அருகு ஒன்று மற்று-இளம் பார்ப்பு‘ என
பசும்பிடி இள முகிழ், நெகிழ்ந்த வாய் ஆம்பல்,
எருவை நறுந் தோடு, எரி இணர் வேங்கை,
உருவம் மிகு தோன்றி, ஊழ் இணர் நறவம்,
பருவம் இல் கோங்கம், பகை மலர் இலவம்;

thinai_evidence.note: the flowering of the god's hill described as praise

comparisons.tenor: the floating buds in the pool

tamil: நின யானைச் சென்னி நிறம் குங்குமத் தால்
புனையா, பூ நீர் ஊட்டி, புனை கவரி சார்த்தா.
பொற் பவழப் பூங் காம்பின் பொற்குடை ஏற்றி,
பல் மணம் மன்னு பின் இருங் கூந்தலர்,
கொடி ஏற்று வாரணம் கொள் கவழ மிச்சில்--
மறு அற்ற மைந்தர் தோள் எய்தார்; மணந்தார்
விரி கதிர் முற்றா விரி சுடர் ஒத்தி;
அவ் வரை உடைத்தோய்! நீ இவ் வரை மருங்கில்

thinai_evidence.note: closing praise and worship of the god, under paadaan

title: வையை (20)
theme: Paripadal 20, the Vaiyai: the rain-borne flood with its scents, the town's comic rush to the river, a wife who finds her bangle on her husband's courtesan, the abuse and the courtesan's reply, the onlookers' counsel that love keeps no bounds, and the river's nature of joining lovers.
source_issues: Paripadal 20: the colophon has no thinai or thurai; it gives the poet நல்லந்துவனார், the music by நல்லச்சுதனார், the pan காந்தாரம் and the subject வையை.

Paripadal 20 line 95 (வையை நீர் மலர்களுடன் வந்து கூடல் மதிலின்) reads as a modern prose heading left in the verse text, not verse; it accounts for the lineation flag at line 96 (printed 95 stands on line 96) and for the core text's 112 lines against the source's 111.
Paripadal 20: the builder dropped lines it took for modern headings at positions 1, 13, 29, 87 and 100 (flags); none could be checked against a second edition in the corpus.
Paripadal 20 lines 72, 73, 74, 87, 88 and 89 are not in sangamtamil.com's text (flag); ours kept.
Paripadal 20 line 74 has a gap (அ...), so the opening of the wife's speech to the courtesan is incomplete.
Paripadal 20 line 13 வேசனை and line 82 கதுவாய் are doubtful readings in our text.

tamil: கடல் குறைபடுத்த நீர் கல் குறைபட எறிந்து,
உடல் ஏறு உருமினம் ஆர்ப்ப, மலை மாலை
பொருது இகல் புலி போழ்ந்த பூ நுதல் எழில் யானைக்
குருதிக் கோட்டு அழி கறை தெளி பெறக் கழீஇயின்று
காலைக் கடல் படிந்து, காய் கதிரோன் போய வழி
மாலை மலை மணந்து, மண் துயின்ற கங்குலான்
வான் ஆற்றும் மழை தலைஇ; மரன் ஆற்றும் மலர் நாற்றம்,
தேன் ஆற்றும் மலர் நாற்றம், செறு வெயில் உறு கால
கான் ஆற்றும் கார் நாற்றம், கொம்பு உதிர்த்த கனி நாற்றம்;
தான், நாற்றம் கலந்து உடன் தழீஇ வந்து, தரூஉம், வையை.
தன் நாற்றம் மீது, தடம் பொழில் தான், யாற்று
reading: Clouds that drank the sea until it shrank break on the hills with roaring thunder, rain on them again and again at evening, wash clean the blood on the tusks of an elephant that fought a tiger, and through the sleeping night pour down, so that the Vaiyai arrives bearing, all mixed together, the scent of tree blossom, of honey flowers, of the rain-soaked forest after scorching summer, and of fruit shaken from the boughs, its own fragrance rising above the river's rank flood smell.
nuance: The opening is a chain of scents (நாற்றம், five times in lines 8 to 13) rather than of sights: the river is known by what it carries from the hills before it is seen. The elephant's tusk washed of a tiger's blood brings hill violence down into the river that will carry the town's play. வேசனை (line 13) is an unusual word in our text.

thinai_evidence.note: the river's coming with the rains is hailed as a gift, praise under paadaan (porul 2.27)

tamil: ஊர்ஊர் பறை ஒலி கொண்டன்று; உயர் மதிலில்
நீர் ஊர் அரவத்தால் துயில் உணர்பு எழீஇ,
ஆடுவார் பொய்தல் அணி வண்டு இமிர் மணல்
கோடு ஏறு எருத்தத்து இரும் புனலில் குறுகி,
reading: Drums sound in town after town; woken by the roar of the water climbing the high wall, people in their haste yoke chariot horses to boats and drive boat-carts as chariots, harness rutting elephants with gear meant for war horses, men put on women's garlands and women men's, all order forgotten in the wish to be first, and they crowd the mansion streets down to the bee-loud sand of the great flood: such is the Vaiyai that Koodal longs for.
nuance: Lines 16 to 21 are a set of crossed pairs (horse and boat, horse-gear and elephant, women's garland and men's), each half reversing the other; the comedy of confusion is also love's mixing, which the closing lines of the poem will name as the river's nature. கூடல் in line 26 is both the town's name and 'union'.

thinai_evidence.note: lovers rush to the river, wearing each other's garlands, the union of the river town

tamil: புகை வகை தைஇயினார் பூங் கோதை நல்லார்,
இயல் அணி, அணி நிற்ப ஏறி; அமர் பரப்பின்
அயல் அயல் அணி நோக்கி--ஆங்கு ஆங்கு வருபவர்
ஓடி ஒளித்து, ஒய்யப் போவாள் நிலை காண்மின்.
நெறி மணல் நேடினர் செல்ல, சொல் ஏற்று,
reading: Women decked in garlands of every kind climb up and look at one another's finery across the crowd, and there a wife, her husband beside her, sees on another woman's body the bangle and necklace he gave away, and, hurt, marks her as the rival; the poet bids us look at the giver, the thief, and his shamed face, and at the other woman running to hide among women whose eyes are like the arrows of battle, slipping away; the wife's women hunt her along the sand, demand what tie she has with him, and she, defiant at first, stands dumb, her wits gone.
nuance: The proof is an object: the bangle the wife lost (கெடு வளை) appears on the rival, so the quarrel that follows is about property as much as love. The poet calls the husband கள்வன், the thief, before anyone in the poem does. Lines 41 to 45 are compressed and the speakers are not named; whether 'மாற்றாள் மகள்' (line 45) is the rival herself or her daughter is unclear.

thinai_evidence.note: a wife finds her own bangle on her husband's other woman, the marutham quarrel

comparisons.tenor: the crowd of women in which she hides

tamil: மாயப் பொய் கூட்டி மயக்கும் விலைக் கணிகை!
துற்றவ துற்றும் துணை இதழ் வாய்த் தொட்டி!
முற்றா நறு நறா மொய் புனல் அட்டி,
காரிகை நீர் ஏர் வயல், காமக் களி நாஞ்சில்,
தட மென் தோள் தொட்டு, தகைத்து, மட விரலால்
இட்டார்க்கு யாழ் ஆர்த்தும் பாணியில், எம் இழையைத்
தொட்டு, ஆர்த்தும் இன்பத் துறைப் பொதுவி! கெட்டதைப்
பொய்தல் மகளிர் கண் காண இகுத்தந்து, இவ்
தன் மார்பம் தண்டம் தரும் ஆரத்தாள் மார்பும்,
நின் மார்பும், ஓர் ஒத்த நீர்மைய கொல்?‘ என்னாமுன்
தேடினாள் ஏச, சில மகளிர் மற்று அதற்கு
reading: One of the wife's company turns on the other woman: a bought courtesan who mixes love with tricks and lies, whose womanhood is common to all, an old vat that pours raw toddy and drives the plough of love's frenzy through the field of beauty, a herdswoman of the pleasure-ford who strings our jewel like a lute for whoever pays; we brought the stray before the bathing women into this Vaiyai pen, broke him, beat him with garlands for a whip and followed him to the assembly, for farmers do not let an ox run off unworked; is your chest the same as hers whose chest wears the necklace he paid as forfeit?; and while she rails, some women take offence at it there in the Vaiyai.
nuance: The abuse is built as a farming allegory: the husband is the household's ox, the courtesan a herdswoman (பொதுவி, also 'woman held in common') who drives him off, and the wife's party the farmers who own the work. The whipping with garlands (மத்திகை மாலையா) turns the river festival's flower-play into a mock punishment. Lines 51, 54 and 64 are obscure in our text.

tamil: மைந்து உற்றாய், வெஞ் சொல்; மட மயிற் சாயலை
வந்திக்க வார்‘ என --- ‘மனத் தகக நோய் இது;
போற்றாய் காண், அன்னை! புரையோய்! புரை இன்று,
எந்தை எனக்கு ஈத்த இடு வளை, ஆரப் பூண்
வந்த வழி நின்பால் மாயக் களவு அன்றேல்,
மாலை அணிய விலை தந்தான்; மாதர் நின்
அதிரல் அம் கண்ணி! நீ அன்பன் எற்கு அன்பன்;
கதுவாய்; அவன் கள்வன்; கள்வி நான் அல்லேன்.‘
reading: Peacemakers ask the wife's side to stop harsh words and go and salute the soft, peacock-graced woman; the answer is that this is a sickness of the heart, that it is shameful for strangers to bow to strangers and unfitting for a rival to go to a rival; the wife tells the silent courtesan that if the bangle and necklace given to her came to her by no trick of theft, let her give back the man who gave them and then be proud; and the courtesan answers that he paid her price for garlands, that he would strip even the anklets from the wife's feet, that the wife's beloved is her beloved too: he is the thief, and she is no thief.
nuance: The courtesan's defence turns the word the poet used at line 36 back on the husband: கள்வன் is his, கள்வி she refuses (line 82). Her claim that he paid (விலை தந்தான்) makes the gift a fair purchase and the wife's ornaments his to give. எந்தை (line 76) may be the wife's father, which would make the bangle her own dowry, or her lord; the reading changes how sharp her charge is. Line 74 has a gap, and line 82 கதுவாய் is obscure.

thinai_evidence.note: wife and courtesan face each other over the husband's gifts

tamil: கட வரை நிற்குமோ காமம்? கொடி இயலாய்!‘
வையை நீர் மலர்களுடன் வந்து கூடல் மதிலின்
reading: The onlookers tell the courtesan, doe of Vachchi, to stop her defiance, since what her lovers give is hers in the sight of the land, and tell the wife that a woman whose husband goes to the sweet beds of others cannot spend her life driving crows away: women of worth, even when their husbands slight their virtue, praise and bow to them, so let her stop, for no one has ever managed to bar the chests of men who chase women, and love does not stay within bounds; such resolves and sulks the Pandya's Vaiyai brings on.
nuance: The counsel is double: it gives the courtesan her gifts by public right (நாடு அறிய நும்மவே) and asks the wife to accept what cannot be stopped, so the ideal of the wife who bows to her husband (lines 88, 89) is offered as resignation, not as a source of power. வச்சிய (line 84) is unclear: a place or a people. Line 95 is a modern prose heading, not verse; lines 87 to 89 are not in sangamtamil.com.

tamil: சினை விரிந்து உதிர்ந்த வீ, புதல் விரி போதொடும்,
நெடு மால் கருங்கை நடு வழிப் போந்து--
கடு மா களிறு அணைத்துக் கைவிடு நீர் போலும்
நெடு நீர் மலி புனல், நீள் மாடக் கூடல்
reading: Buds folded like the hands of slender women, clusters spread like angry serpents' hoods, flowers opened like parasols, water flowers swept out of the pools, blossoms fallen from the boughs and buds from the bushes, all driven on by the waves the waterfalls poured, come down the middle way, and the full flood falls on the guarded wall of tall-mansioned Koodal like water that a fierce bull elephant holds in its trunk and lets go; and it is the nature of the flower-filled Vaiyai to bring lovers together to play, so that quarrel, friendship, parting, love and toddy are all mixed and praised as one.
nuance: The close makes the quarrel of the middle of the poem part of the river's gift: the list in lines 109 and 110 puts the fight and the parting beside friendship and love, so the bitter exchange of wife and courtesan is counted among the festival's pleasures. The hill flowers come down to the town's wall, so kurinji things end in a marutham scene. நெடு மால் கருங்கை (line 105) is obscure in our text.

title: செவ்வேள் / வையை (21, 22)
theme: Paripadal 21, to Sevvel at Parankunram: the god named by what he rides, wears, holds and dwells on, the hill's women in their sulks and adornments seen as a painting, the hill's creatures as an orchestra, a husband's plunge after his wife in a pool, and a wife's dance to her husband's drum before the prayer to dwell at his feet; and Paripadal 22, to the Vaiyai, broken by gaps: the rain told as the king's war and gifts, the procession to the bank, lovers who may be the river's ornament or it theirs, and the sounds of the Thirumarutham ford.
source_issues: Paripadal 21 and 22: the colophons have no thinai or thurai; 21's pan is காந்தாரம, a musical mode, and 22 has no poet, music or pan (தெரியவில்லை).
Paripadal 21 line 30 and 22 line 17: a line was taken for a modern heading and dropped before them (flags); not checked by eye.
Paripadal 21 lines 9 and 21 and 22 line 7 are repaired from sangamtamil.com's reading (flags); 21 line 11 has ஒன்ணுபடு, likely a misprint.
Paripadal 22 lines 10, 12, 14, 15, 20, 37, 42, 47 and 50 have gaps; line 50 has no Tamil letters, and line 13 (கான மலைத்தரை கொன்று மணல பினறி) and line 17 (பொறிவி யாற்றுறி) are garbled.
Paripadal 22 lines 18, 19, 37, 38 and 39 are not in sangamtamil.com's text; the flag that line 1 differs strongly compares it with 21's line 63, so sangamtamil.com's alignment is off by a song there.

tamil: ஊர்ந்ததை--எரி புரை ஓடை இடை இமைக்கும் சென்னி,
பொரு சமம் கடந்த புகழ் சால், வேழம்.
தொட்டதை--தைப்பு அமை சருமத்தின், தாள் இயை தாமரை
துப்பு அமை துவர் நீர்த் துறை மறை அழுத்திய,
வரி மலி அர உரி வள்பு கண்டன்ன,
புரி மென் பீலிப் போழ் புனை அடையல்.
புள்ளொடு பெயரிய பொருப்புப் புடை திறந்த வேல்;
உருள் இணர்க் கடம்பின் ஒன்ணுபடு கமழ் தார்.
நிரை ஏழ் அடுக்கிய நீள் இலைப் பாலை
அரை வரை மேகலை, அளி நீர்ச் சூழி,
வென்றிக் கொடி அணி வெல்வ! நிற் தொழுது.
reading: The poet names the god's possessions one by one, what he rides (a war elephant famed for battles won, a fire-bright frontlet flashing on its head), what he has put on (a garment of stitched hide and strips of soft peacock feather, worked like a striped snakeskin strap), what is in his hand (the spear that cut down the mango trunk of the unyielding foe and split open the hill named after a bird), what he wears (a fragrant garland of round kadamba clusters woven through with curling valli creeper) and what he has settled on (cool Parankunram, praised on the tongues of the worthy, girdled at its waist by seven rows of long-leaved paalai trees, with pools of sweet water, a hill that earth and sky delight in), and prays, worshipping the victor with the banner, that dwelling at the foot of that hill be granted.
nuance: The unit is a catechism: five neuter nouns (ஊர்ந்ததை, தொட்டதை, கையதை, பூண்டதை, அமர்ந்ததை, 'what he rode, touched, held, wore, settled on') each answered in turn, and the last answer is a place, so the hill is counted among the god's belongings like his spear and garland. The prayer asks for nothing but residence: குன்றத்து அடி, the foot of the hill, also reads as the god's feet. Lines 3 to 7, the garment, are compressed and their syntax is a reading.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god by his mount, dress, weapon, garland and hill, a கடவுள் வாழ்த்து under paadaan (porul 2.27)

comparisons.tenor: the gold frontlet on the elephant's brow
the strips of the god's garment
