tamil: சுடு பொன் ஞெகிழத்து முத்து அரி சென்று ஆர்ப்ப,
துடியின் அடி பெயர்த்து, தோள் அசைத்துத் தூக்கி,
அடு நறா மகிழ் தட்ப ஆடுவாள் தகைமையின்,
அழல் புனை அவிர் இழை திருத்துவாள் குறிப்பும்;
பல் ஊழ் இவை இவை நினைப்பின், வல்லோன்
reading: On the god's hill one woman, dancing with anklets of gold whose pearl pellets ring as she steps to the drum and swings her arms, held back by the joy of brewed toddy, turns eyes red as a bright spear point on the husband who would embrace her and sulks; another looks into a mirror to see her reflection and sets right her fire-bright jewels; another smears sandal between her swelling breasts, rubs it off, and wants it applied again; thought over and over, says the poet to the god who cut down the mango, these scenes are like the beauty a master paints in a picture.
nuance: The three women are given as states (நிலையும், குறிப்பும், விருப்பும்: her stance, her intent, her desire), so the poet paints moods, not deeds, and calls the whole a painting; the sulk, the mirror and the sandal are the household's oodal and toilet carried up to the shrine hill. Line 26 (பின் உற ஊட்டுவாள்) is compressed, and who is to apply the sandal again is our reading; line 21 is a repaired line.

thinai_evidence.note: a woman sulking at her husband, marutham's uri, set on the kurinji hill of the god

comparisons.tenor: the women's moods seen on the hill

tamil: இசை படு பக்கம், இரு பாலும் கோலி,
விடு பொறி மஞ்ஞை பெயர்பு உடன் ஆட;
விரல் செறி தூம்பின் விடு துளைக்கு ஏற்ப,
முரல் குரற் தும்பி அவிழ் மலர் ஊத;
பாணி முழவு இசை அருவி நீர் ததும்ப;
reading: On the hill of the god with the resounding drum, everything sounds at once: the spotted peacock, spreading its tail on both sides like a fan raised overhead at the thunder of the cloud, dances; the humming thumbi blows into the opened flowers as a flute is blown through the holes the fingers close; the new-come swarms of bees bring forth the music of the lute; and the waterfall brims with the sound of the beating drum.
nuance: No human player is named: the hill itself is the orchestra, peacock for dancer, thumbi for flute, bees for lute, falls for drum, and the only drum that is a drum is the god's own (இரங்கு முரசினான்), so the god is named by the one instrument the creatures answer. A line before line 30 may have been dropped as a heading (flag).

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god's hill as a place where every creature sounds together, under paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the hum of the bee swarms

tamil: தாழ் நீர் இமிழ் சுனை நாப்பண் குளித்து, அவண்
வேய் நீர் அழுந்து தன் கையின் விடுக என,
பூ நீர் பெய் வட்டம் எறிய, புணை பெறாது
அரு நிலை நீரின் அவள் துயர் கண்டு,
கொழுநன் மகிழ் தூங்கி, கொய் பூம் புனல் வீழ்ந்து,
கயல் புரை கண்ணியர் கமழ் துகள் உதிர்த்த
பசும் பூண் சேஎய்!-நின் குன்றம் நன்கு உடைத்து.
reading: A woman in fine jewels who has bathed in the middle of a deep, echoing pool rises above the water; in the play, as a bowl of flower-water is flung, she has no float and is in distress in the deep water, and her husband, seeing it, giddy with joy, drops into the flower-strewn water and embraces her: such is cool Parankunram; and the god's hill, its falls spreading over steep clefts, has these winds in plenty, the wind mixed with the cool fragrant sandal that young men rubbed on, the wind that stirred the cloud-dark hair of fish-eyed women and shook out its scented dust, and the wind that passed through the fragrant smoke raised for the tall Vel of the kadamba.
nuance: The three winds (வளியும் three times) carry the hill's three kinds of scent, men's sandal, women's hair, the god's incense, so lovers and worship are one air on the hill. The rescue in the pool turns a moment of danger into the embrace, the husband's joy (மகிழ் தூங்கி) coming before he plunges. Lines 40 to 42 are hard: who is told to let go of whom (கேள்வனை ... விடுக) and who throws the bowl is our reading.

thinai_evidence.note: a husband's embrace of his wife in a pool on the hill: union, with the things of the kurinji hill

tamil: கண் ஒளிர் திகழ் அடர், இடுசுடர் படர் கொடி மின்னுப் போல்,
ஒண் நகை தகை வகை நெறிபெற இடைஇடை இழைத்து யாத்த
மணி மருள் தேன் மகிழ் தட்ப, ஒல்கிப்
பிணி நெகிழப் பைந் துகில், நோக்கம் சிவப்பு ஊர,
பூங் கொடி போல நுடங்குவாள், ஆங்குத் தன்
கோடு அணிந்த முத்து ஆரம் ஒல்க ஓசிபவள் ஏர்-
ஆடை அசைய, அணி அசைய, தான் அசையும்
மாறு அமர் அட்டவை மற வேல் பெயர்ப்பவை;
ஆறு இரு தோளவை; அறு முகம் விரித்தவை;
நன்று அமர் ஆயமோடு ஒருங்கு, ‘நின் அடி உறை
reading: A woman whose chaplet, set at intervals with bright gold plates flashing like a creeper of lightning, falls along her hair, held back by honey liquor like a gem, sways, her green cloth loosening and her eyes reddening, bending like a flowering creeper to the beat of the drum her worthy husband rolls, her pearl chain swaying on her breasts, her cloth swaying, her ornaments swaying and she swaying like a branch ruffled by the north wind; her eyes as she shifts her shoulders to the drum are like rolling arrows; and the poet, hailing the god who wielded the fierce spear that won the battle, of twelve shoulders and six spread faces, prays with his glad company that their dwelling at the god's feet be granted as it is today, worshipping the lord who wore down his foes.
nuance: The husband plays the drum and the wife dances, so a married pair performs the hill's rite together, and the prayer at the close asks that 'today' recur (இன்று போல் இயைக), the same refrain as line 16 with the hill's foot now the god's feet. Lines 66 and 67 may continue the woman's eyes (that drive the spear, as his do) or turn to the god in epithets; we read them as epithets.

thinai_evidence.note: a wife's dance to her husband's drum is held inside the closing praise and prayer, so the unit is paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the gold plates in her chaplet
the woman swaying with cloth and ornaments
her eyes moving to the drum

tamil: ஒளிறு வாட் பொருப்பன் உடல் சமத்து இறுத்த
விடும் கணை ஒப்பின் கதழ் உறை சிதறூஉ,
கண் ஒளிர் எஃகின் கடிய மின்னி, அவன்
போன நிலம் எல்லாம் போர் ஆர் வயல் புகுத-
reading: Clouds press on like the rows of elephants that the shining-sworded lord of hills halted in the battle where bodies fell; thunder rolls like the drum of the one of unceasing wrath who overcame kings; the rain falls scattering swift drops like the arrows loosed by the bows of his army against the unyielding; lightning flashes fierce as his gleaming spear; and the water the sky poured like his bounty gathers on the earth without stopping and, like his army, enters all the land where it went, the fields full of sheaves; the rest of the passage, broken by gaps, speaks of hills and sand, a drum beaten, and the flood coming on head to head in strength.
nuance: Every part of the storm is copied from the king: his elephants, drum, arrows, spear and, last, his giving, so the monsoon that makes the Vaiyai is told as the king's war and the king's bounty at once, and the flood that enters the fields is his army taking ground. Lines 10 and 12 to 15 have gaps, and line 13 is garbled.

thinai_evidence.note: the river's rain and flood praised through the king's war and gifts, under paadaan

tamil: நறவு அணி பூந் துகில் நன் பல ஏந்தி,
செறி வினைப் பொலிந்த செம் பூங் கண்ணியர்,
ஈர் அமை வெட்சி இதழ் புனை கோதையர்,
தார் ஆர் முடியர், தகை கெழு மார்பினர்;
reading: People come carrying red dye, incense and sandal paste, things fit for the wet-dress of the bathing, and many fine flowered cloths, with others following behind; women with red flower chaplets of close work and garlands of petals of fresh vetchi, men with garlands and crowns and handsome chests; and horses, elephants and gem-adorned mules crowd the bank and fill the groves.
nuance: ஈரணி, the dress for wet play, names a festival kit: things are brought to be worn in the water. Line 17 is garbled after a dropped heading and line 20 has a gap, so the opening of the list is our reading.

thinai_evidence.note: the town's procession to the river for the festival bathing, praise of the river's day under paadaan

tamil: வேல் ஆற்றும் பொய்ம்பனின், விரை மலர் அம்பினோன்
போல், ஆற்று முன்பின் புனை கழல் மைந்தரொடு,
தார் அணி மைந்தர் தவப் பயன் ஆம் எனக்
கார் அணி கூந்தல், கயற் கண், கவிர் இதழ்,
வார் அணி கொம்மை, வகை அமை மேகலை,
ஏர் அணி இலங்கு எயிற்று, இலங்கு நகையவர்-
நீர் அணி நீத்தம் இவர்க்கு அணிகொல்? எனத்
reading: With young men in warrior anklets, strong as the god who wields the spear and lovely as the god of the fragrant flower arrows, come women counted the fruit of the garlanded men's penance, with hair dark as the rain cloud, carp eyes, lips like the kavir flower, long-banded breasts, girdles of fine work and bright teeth and smiles; those who try to judge ask whether these are an ornament to the famed Vaiyai or the Vaiyai's ornamented flood an ornament to them, and cannot decide: such is the beauty where the bank and the Vaiyai meet.
nuance: The praise is a doubt that will not resolve (தேர்தற்கு அரிது): the river and the women each seem the other's ornament, so the festival beauty belongs to neither alone but to their meeting (தீரமும் வையையும் சேர்கின்ற). The men are given two gods for models at once, Murugan for strength and Kama for beauty.

thinai_evidence.note: lovers on the river bank, the women as the reward of the men's penance: union by the river

comparisons.vehicle: வேல் ஆற்றும் பொய்ம்பனின், விரை மலர் அம்பினோன்

tamil: மண் கணை முழவின் இன் கண் இமிழ்விற்கு
கவர் தொடை நல் யாழ் இமிழ, காவில்
புகர் வரி வண்டினம் பூஞ் சினை இமிர,
தாது ஊது தும்பி தவிர்பு அல இயம்ப,
ஆங்கு அவை தத்தம் தொழில் மாறு கொள்ளும்-
கோடுளர் குரல் பொலி ஒலி துயல் இருங் கூந்தல்,
தோள் தாழ்பு தழை மலர் துவளா வல்லியின்,
நீள் தாழ்பு தோக்கை, நித்தில வரிச் சிலம்பு,
reading: To the sweet beat of the earth-clay drum something answers sound for sound (the line is broken), the lute of forked strings sounds, in the grove the spotted swarms of bees hum on the flowering branches, the sweet flute plays its measure, the thumbi sipping pollen on the flowers sounds without pause, and, as the hand drum keeps time, the wind, a dancer, makes the soft-clustered flowering creeper sway: so at the Thirumarutham ford of the sweet-watered Vaiyai all these take up each other's work; then, in broken lines, a woman is described, dark heavy hair swinging, long soft shoulders drooping like a creeper whose leaves and flowers do not wilt, a long trailing cloth and anklets striped with pearls.
nuance: தத்தம் தொழில் மாறு கொள்ளும், 'they exchange their work', is the point: at the ford the town's instruments and the grove's creatures answer each other, the wind takes the dancer's part and the bees the singer's. Lines 37, 42, 47 and 50 are broken, and the woman of lines 46 to 50 cannot be fully read.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the sounds at the river's sacred ford, under paadaan

title: திருமால் (thirattu:1)
theme: Thirumal at Irunthaiyur by Koodal: the ford, the ring of hill, pond and field, the peoples and shrines of his town, and the serpent lord whose deeds are its glory (Paripadal Thirattu 1).
source_issues: Paripadal Thirattu 1: the colophon gives no thinai, thurai, poet or pan; only the subject திருமால் is recorded, and the song is a fragment preserved outside the main collection.
Paripadal Thirattu 1: our text has 86 lines but the source numbers its last line 82, and printed line number 45 stands on line 44 (lineation flag); line numbers here are the ones show prints.

Paripadal Thirattu 1 lines 49 and 60 were flagged as possible modern headings (heading_dropped), but both are verse: line 49 opens the run of ஆர்ப்ப / அதிர / ஆர்ப்ப clauses (49-51), and line 60 continues the string of the women's attributes (59-61); kept.
Paripadal Thirattu 1 lines 1-14 are not in sangamtamil.com (flag), and the யொடு restoration in line 14 (இசையொடு) is by rule, unconfirmed there.

Paripadal Thirattu 1 line 32: the repair flag reports பேரிசை restored on this line, but the line as printed (கடிப் புகு வேரிக் கதவமிற் றோட்டி) has no such word; the flag may belong to a different line given the lineation drift. The line is obscure.

Paripadal Thirattu 1 lines 30 and 31 repeat almost word for word (வண்டு பொரேரென எழ / எழும்), possibly a dittography; line 26 (விளைவதை வினை எவன்) and lines 59-63 and 74-77 are hard to construe and readings there are tentative.

tamil: வான் ஆர் எழிலி மழை வளம் நந்த,
மருந்து ஆகும் தீம் நீர் மலி துறை மேய
பிணி நெகிழ் பிண்டி, நிவந்து சேர்பு ஓங்கி,
வண்ண வரி இதழ்ப் போதின்வாய் வண்டு ஆர்ப்ப,
விண் வீற்றிருக்கும் கய மீன் விரி தகையின்
reading: Where the river, swollen by the rain of the sky-filling clouds, comes down from the honeyed peaks and is met by four-towered Koodal, at the ghat brimming with sweet water that is a medicine, the singers bow their heads to the well-formed feet of the lord seated at Irunthaiyur and praise him; around him lie, on one side, a hill gone gem-dark with vengai, maraa, makizham and opening asoka trees, on another a pond whose lotus buds hum with bees and whose flowers sit in it like the stars spread in the sky, and on another fields where ploughing noise rivals the festival music of the flood, revellers wander dazed and planters shout, fields fit for the goddess of fortune to desire.
nuance: The shrine is placed by water before it is placed by anything else: the river is not named, only traced from rain to hill to the city's welcome, and the ghat's water is called a medicine (மருந்து ஆகும் தீம் நீர், line 4), so the holiness of the site begins as the healing of its ford. The ஒருசார் (on one side) refrain that begins at line 7 lays out the god's surroundings as a ring of landscapes, hill, pond and field, each closed by a one-word line (மலை, கயம், வயல்).

thinai_evidence.note: worship of the god seated at Irunthaiyur, opened by bowing at his feet: கடவுள் வாழ்த்து under paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the hill dark with massed trees
the lotus flowers sitting in the pond

tamil: பண்ணியம், மாசு அறு பயம் தரு காருகப்
விளைவதை வினை எவன் மென் புல வன் புலக்
ஆங்க அனையவை நல்ல நனி கூடும் இன்பம்
reading: On one side is the settlement that does not swerve from aram, where brahmins gather who have completed the penance joined to aram and the Veda, whose fame of mastery stands and who never stray in the way of their learning by hearing; on another the decked street of meritorious merchants and weavers, selling what is eaten, smeared, worn, put on and washed with, gems and gold, the goods of hill and sea and wares that yield clean profit; on another the guarded street of the field hands and ploughmen of soft and hard lands; and on every side such good things meet, so that delight comes in its proper measure.
nuance: The catalogue gives each people its virtue in the word that names it: the brahmins' settlement does not swerve from aram (அறத்தின் திரியா, line 21), the merchants are புண்ணிய வணிகர் (line 25), meritorious traders, and the farmers' street is guarded (கடி மறுகு). Merit is assigned to trade as well as to rite, so the shrine town is pictured as a whole social order, not a priestly enclave. Line 26 (விளைவதை வினை எவன்) does not construe as it stands.

thinai_evidence.note: the god's town praised through the peoples gathered round the shrine, still within the hymn: paadaan

tamil: கடிப்பு இகு காதில் கனம் குழை தொடர-
மிளிர் மின் வாய்ந்த விளங்கு ஒளி நுதலார்
வாய் இருள் பனிச்சை வரி சிலைப் புருவத்து
reading: As the bees rise with a rush, there crowd without pause at the shrine of the lord of the hill, whose neck bears the two-coloured mark, the devotees: women with heavy ear-rings and brows bright as lightning, men noble as those who ride elephants, women with dark plaits and bow-curved brows, men adorned with a fame that matches their learning, women adorned with a modesty that matches their beauty, men whose victorious gait rivals the bull, women of gentle gait, old men grey as the ranked waves of the sea, bearing food offerings, umbrellas, incense and flowers, so that the town is like the unshaken heaven where those whose deeds have ripened enjoy their great fruit.
nuance: The crowd is drawn in matched pairs, each man's line answered by a woman's (fame matched to learning against modesty matched to beauty, lines 38 and 39; the bull's gait against the gait of innocence, lines 40 and 41), so the worshippers are a society of couples before they are a congregation. The heaven the town resembles is one of enjoyment earned by ripened deeds (விளைந்தார் வினையின் விழுப் பயன் துய்க்கும், line 45), not of release. Who the lord of the hill is (lines 47, 48) is not certain; the two-coloured mark on the neck (உத்தி) may be the spots of a serpent's hood, which would tie this shrine to the serpent lord of lines 83 and 84. Lines 30 to 32 are obscure.

thinai_evidence.note: the crowd of devotees at the hill lord's shrine: worship, paadaan

comparisons.tenor: the grey hair of the old
the hill lord's town crowded with devotees

tamil: வண்டொடு தும்பியும் வண் தொடை யாழ் ஆர்ப்ப,
மணி மருள் தகை வகை நெறி செறி ஒலி பொலி அவிர் நிமிர் புகழ் கூந்தல்
பிணி நெகிழ் துளையினை தெளி ஒளி திகழ் ஞெகிழ் தெரி அரி
மது மகிழ்பு அரி மலர் மகிழ் உண்கண், வாணுதலோர்-
மணி மயில் தொழில் எழில் இகல் மலி திகழ் பிறிது
அணி மிக வந்து இறைஞ்ச, அல் இகப்ப, பிணி நீங்க,
வரை வாய் தழுவிய கல் சேர் கிடக்கைக்
reading: With bees and humming beetles and the well-strung lute resounding, the musth elephant trumpeting with the thunder of the clouds, the twin drums sounding with the unceasing falls, men joined with women whose eyes are streaked red, dance appearing with well-wrought song, garland buds opening with the honey that is worn and desire wanting more with the toddy that is not, all these and others like them meet in the town of the Nagas with flowered crowns; and in the town of the one seated at Kulavaay, on the stony bed that hugs the hill's mouth, women with gem-like rippling hair, anklets and flower-like eyes come richly adorned with lords like musth elephants and bow, the darkness passes, affliction leaves and all good things come together.
nuance: Lines 54 and 55 play on one word: the honey that is worn (சூடு நறவு) opens the garland buds, the honey that is not worn, the drunk toddy, makes desire grow; the shrine festival is openly a festival of drink and love, and the poem lists it among the things that befit the god's town without apology. Both shrines end on a நகர் line (58, 67), continuing the shrine-by-shrine walk of lines 47 and 48. Lines 59 to 63 are long strings of attributes that are hard to divide.

thinai_evidence.note: festivals at two shrines of the god's town, sung as praise: paadaan

tamil: திகழ் ஒளி முந்நீர் கடைந்த அக் கால், வெற்புத்
திகழ்பு எழ வாங்கித் தம் சீர்ச் சிரத்து ஏற்றி,
அமுது கடைய, இரு வயின் நாண் ஆகி,
அணிபோல் பொறுத்தாரும் தாஅம்; பணிபு இல் சீர்ச்
கல் உயர் வென்னி இமய வில் நாண் ஆகித்
reading: When the bright ocean was churned, it was they who drew up the mountain, bore it on their own heads and set it in the sea of leaping makaras, who for the two famed hosts became the rope at both ends while the discus-bearer pulled the twin cords, and wore it unbroken through ages with strength that did not give; it was they who met head-on all the overwhelming might that came against them; they who bore like an ornament the earth on which the great gem-like mountains stand; and they who, when the rider of the bull destroyed the three cities, became the string of the Himalaya bow and gave it its ancient fame: bowing to that lord with his host who spreads a thousand awful heads and extolling his good feet, we praise you, and ask that none of us be parted, all together with our kin.
nuance: Each deed closes on தாம் (they themselves, lines 75, 77, 79, 82), so the churning, the bearing of the earth and the bowstring of the three-city war, which other poems give to Mal or to Shiva, are counted here as the serpent's own fame (தொல் புகழ் தந்தாரும் தாம்). The serpent lord is bowed to first and the god praised through him (நல் அடி ஏத்தி நிற் பரவுதும், line 85), a shrine-order of attendant before master. The closing wish is not for release but that the worshippers and their kin stay together. Line 74 (ஒரு தோழம் காலம்) and lines 76 and 77 are hard to construe.

thinai_evidence.note: the serpent's deeds told as praise and the closing prayer: paadaan

title: வையை (thirattu:2)
theme: Paripadal thirattu 2, the Vaiyai fragment: the rain-fed flood reaches Koodal, the whole city rides out to the ford, lovers quarrel over garlands the water carries, the priests refuse the stained river, the bathing at the royal ford of Tirumarutham, and Maran in the flood likened to Indra in the river of the sky.
source_issues: Thirattu 2 line 4 reads சுடுகின்றே, which gives no sense in context; சூடுகின்றே (wears, crowns) is likely.
Thirattu 2 line 11 கண்னியர் and line 100 கன்ணினான் show ன for ண (கண்ணியர், கண்ணினான்); kept as written.
Thirattu 2 line 41 கயத் தகக is corrupt (perhaps கயத்துத் தக்க); line 84 மழுபொடு cannot be construed.

Thirattu 2: the core text has 101 lines but the source numbers its last line 96, and printed line 65 stands on line 67 (flags); the short half-lines 65, 67, 69 and 71 are probably the unnumbered ones.
Thirattu 2: the builder dropped lines it took for modern headings at positions 5 and 65 (flags); not checked against a second edition.
Thirattu 2 lines 29, 72 and 73 are not in sangamtamil.com's text (flag); ours kept.
Thirattu 2: the colophon has no thinai, thurai, poet or pan; the fragment survives without its frame.

tamil: மா நிலம் தோன்றாமை மலி பெயல் தலைஇ,
ஏம நீர் எழில் வானம் இகுத்தரும் பொழுதினான்,
நாக நீள் மணி வரை நறு மலர் பல விரைஇ,
சேர் அணி கொண்டு, நிறம் ஒன்று வெவ்வேறு
reading: When heavy rain has poured from the lovely sky so that the wide land vanishes, the Vaiyai comes down gathering many fragrant flowers from the tall gem-bright hill of Naagam to Koodal; the town, glad that the river has put on its ornament of water, puts on garlands and every finery, each person outdoing the next, and the market is filled with wares of every colour.
nuance: The word அணி (ornament) rings through lines 5 to 10: the river is adorned with water, the people with garlands, the town with its dress, the market with goods, so river and city dress for each other before anyone bathes. Line 4 reads சுடுகின்றே, which gives no sense; சூடுகின்றே (Koodal wears the Vaiyai like a garland) fits the line of ornament imagery but is a correction.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the river and the town that goes out to meet its flood

tamil: பொய்யாம் போய் என்னாப் புடை கூட்டிப் போவநர்
reading: Women soft as tender shoots ride out on decked elephants, with garlands in their hands, wreaths, fine scent, dress, oiled hair and tied locks; others go beside prancing horses or harness carts and chariots, wrap themselves against the heat, make up their quarrels, dance, sing, shout, laugh, run and tire and search for their own people, until no one is left wandering in the town: the learned and the unlearned, the base, parents, wives who never fail their husbands, the king of the golden chariot and gold-walled Koodal itself crowd the Vaiyai's ford.
nuance: The list in lines 24 to 27 deliberately levels the city: learning and its lack, the low and the chaste, the king and the walls themselves, all end at one ford, and line 23 says that nobody stays behind. Lines 18 and 19 are hard to construe in our text; the reading of them as people wrapping against the heat is a guess.

thinai_evidence.note: the whole city, king included, going out to the ford: festival praise, not a love situation

tamil: பிறை ஏர் நுதலியர் எல்லாரும் தம் முன்
இகல் பல செல்வம் விளைத்தவட் கண்டு, இப்பால்,
காதலான் மார்பின் கமழ் தார், புனல் வாங்கி,
தா தா' என்றாளுக்குத்,' தானே புறன் தந்து
நோதலே செய்யேன், நுணங்கு இழையாய்! இச் செவ்வி
கயத் தகக பூப் பெய்த காமக் கிழமை
நீரும் அவட்குத் துணை; கண்ணின் நீர் விட்டோய்!
reading: At the ford where lovers bathe with each other's shoulders for rafts, the crescent-browed women, not seeing who bathes in secret, each take whatever happens before them to be about themselves; one, seeing the flood carry the fragrant garland from her lover's chest into a stranger's hair, cries 'give it, give it', and the other answers that the flood itself turned and set it there: why should she grieve at what fell out, would such a chance come twice, the river joined it knowingly, what a wonder; and the weeping woman is told that the rival's young breasts and the water serve the other's embrace, and that her own tears serve it too.
nuance: The rival's defence makes the flood an accomplice that 'knew' what it was doing (அறிந்து புனல் புணர்த்தது), so the festival river replaces the go-between of the akam poems. The last lines turn on the wife: her tears, like the water, only help the other woman, a hard comfort that tells her weeping is a loss in the quarrel. The speakers are not named and line 41 (கயத் தகக) is corrupt, so the division of voices is a reading.

thinai_evidence.note: a woman finds her lover's garland in a rival's hair and demands it: the marutham quarrel

comparisons.tenor: the lovers' shoulders bearing up those who bathe

tamil: பணிவு இல் உயர் சிறப்பின் பஞ்சவன் கூடல்,
மணி எழில், மா மேனி, முத்த முறுவல்,
அணி பவளச் செவ் வாய், அறம் காவற் பெண்டிர்
மணி அணிந்த தம் உரிமை மைந்தரோடு ஆடித்
புனலூடு நாடு அறியப் பூ மாலை அப்பி,
reading: In the Pandya's unbowed Koodal the wives who guard virtue, gem-fair, dark-bodied, pearl-smiling and coral-lipped, play without pause in the Vaiyai's flood with their own jewelled husbands; and one woman, saying that a garland drifting down the flood came to her hair-knot by the turn of fate, takes it and wears it plainly for the land to see, with a heat that wounds the hearts of those who love; before the lovers meet the sulk grows cruel, and once they meet will she not sulk? The gossip of the town comes and spreads.
nuance: The unit sets two kinds of women in one flood: the wives who guard aram and bathe with their own husbands, and the woman who wears a floating garland as fate's gift so that everyone may see it. The open wearing is the point: what the river delivers by chance becomes a public sign, and the town's அலர் follows. Lines 51 to 56 are knotted in our text and the reading of who sulks is not secure.

thinai_evidence.note: a garland worn openly from the flood brings sulking and the town's gossip

tamil: 'ஈப் பாய் அடு நறாக் கொண்டது, இவ் யாறு' எனப்
விரைபு இரை விரை துறை கரை அழிபு இழிபு ஊர
நுரையுடன் மதகுதொறு இழிதரு புனல் கரை புரளிய
புகும் அளவுஅளவு இயல் இசை சிறை தணிவின்று,
reading: Saying that the river has taken in brewed toddy that bees swarm over, the brahmins give up their dip; saying that it carries the wedding scents young men and women have scattered, the anthanar will not bathe; saying that the Vaiyai is slimy with honey, the aiyar will not even rinse their mouths; and the flood, rushing, roaring, breaking the banks and pouring down, piles foam in rows between bank, hill and sea, spills over every sluice and rolls on to the sea, overflowing every dam.
nuance: Three names for the priestly class (பார்ப்பார், அந்தணர், ஐயர்) each refuse for a different stain, toddy, lovers' scent and honey, and each stain is a sign of the festival the rest of the town is enjoying: what bars the priest is what makes the river a feast. Lines 64 to 71 stack verbs and nouns without connectives so that the sound runs like the water; the short lines 65, 67, 69 and 71 are probably the half-lines the source leaves unnumbered.

thinai_evidence.note: the brahmins' abstention and the flood's overflow, described as festival scene

tamil: வரை பல புரை உயர் கயிறு அணி பயில் தொழில்
மணி அணி யானை மிசை, மைந்தரும் மடவாரும்,
குரு மணி யானை இயல் தேர்ப் பொருநன்
தெரி மருதம் பாடுப, பிணி கொள் யாழ்ப் பாணர்,
reading: On jewelled elephants tall as many hills, young men and women gather in rows and go together to the front ford of Tirumarutham of the king of the gem-hung elephants and chariots, where bards with tight-strung lutes sing the chosen marutham mode; singing and singing, bathing and bathing in the leaping flood, sulking and sulking, longing to be won back, uniting again and again, glad and glad, searching and searching, worn and worn, wearing flowers and bowing again and again, the good women and men bathe in the full Vaiyai until it seems to roar, and the water, the poet tells the worthies of the east, has been wholly used, left like leavings.
nuance: Lines 78 to 83 double every verb (பாடிப் பாடி, ஆடி ஆடி, ஊடி ஊடி, கூடிக் கூடி) so the cycle of sulking and reunion becomes the rhythm of the bathing itself, sung to the marutham mode that belongs to that quarrel. Lines 84 to 87 are obscure: மழுபொடு is not a word we can fix, and the address குணக்குச் சான்றீர் and the close on leavings (மிச்சிலா) are read tentatively.

thinai_evidence.note: the bathing at the royal ford is told as sulking and reunion again and again

tamil: மழை நீர் அறு குளத்து வாய்பூசி ஆடும்
வெரு வரு கொல் யானை வீங்கு தோள் மாறன்,
இரு முந்நீர் வையம் பிடித்து என்னை? யான் ஊர்க்கு
ஒரு நிலையும் ஆற்ற இயையா! அரு மரபின்,
reading: Apart from sandal paste, fragrant garlands, wreaths, scented powder and the flowers slipped from women's hair and men's locks, the water of this Vaiyai shows no colour of its own: it is not clean water but the run-off, cloudy with saffron and bath paste, of those who rinse their mouths at the rain-filled tank and bathe; and when one weighs how Maran of the swelling shoulders and the dreaded killing elephants bathed in the coming flood with the fierce people of Koodal, what is holding the sea-girt world beside it? it is like Indra of the thousand eyes bathing in the river of the high sky.
nuance: The closing praise turns the impurity the priests shunned (lines 58 to 63) into glory: the river has no colour but the town's ornaments, and the king bathing in that very water is likened to Indra in the heavenly river. Lines 98 and 99 (இரு முந்நீர் வையம் பிடித்து என்னை? யான் ஊர்க்கு ஒரு நிலையும் ஆற்ற இயையா) are uncertain; they may mean that ruling the whole world is nothing beside this bathing, or that the speaker cannot match the sight with any state of the town.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the Pandya bathing with his people, likened to Indra

comparisons.tenor: Maran bathing in the Vaiyai with the people of Koodal

title: வையை / திரட்டு / மதுரை (thirattu:3, thirattu:4, thirattu:5, thirattu:6, thirattu:7, thirattu:8, thirattu:9, thirattu:10, thirattu:11, thirattu:12, thirattu:13)
theme: Eleven fragments of lost Paripadal songs, kept by later writers: a prayer to the Vaigai, the flood likened to the Pandya's cavalry, a dancer or bride and her ornaments, and a run of city praises in which Koodal outweighs the world, is laid out as Mayon's lotus, outlasts the king's hill, river and word, outranks heaven by honouring giver and receiver, and bewilders its own people with pleasures.
source_issues: Paripadal thirattu 3 line 2 is lost (a line of dots); the link between the guardians of the scripture in line 1 and the prayer of lines 3 to 5 is gone.
Paripadal thirattu 6 line 3 has a gap before ...னந்து; the end of the sentence is lost.
Paripadal thirattu 4 line 1 and thirattu 5 line 2: TSCII leftovers repaired (flags).
Paripadal thirattu 8 line 11 (கோழியின் எழாது, எம் பேர் ஊர் துயிலே) is not in sangamtamil.com's text; ours kept (flag).
Paripadal thirattu 3 to 13 are fragments with no colophon thinai or thurai; the subject field (வையை, மதுரை) is given for only three of them, though thirattu 8 to 13 are also about Madurai.

reading: With the righteous there to guard the rare scripture, the speaker prays that the close bond between us, which no enemy could wish to break, be joined to us again in the next round as well, and that the cool-flowing Vaigai of excellent course be ours.
nuance: மறுமுறை may mean the next birth or simply the next turn of the festival, when the bathers hope to come to the river again; the lost line 2 kept whatever joined the guardians of the scripture to the prayer, so the bond (நங் கேண்மை) may be the lovers' or the worshippers' with the river.

thinai_evidence.note: a closing prayer addressed through the river, the vaazhthu of paadaan

reading: The Vaigai spread out like the ranks of horses of the Pandya, lord of the southern mountain, who is versed in the threefold Tamil.
nuance: The king is named not by conquest but by learning (தெரிமாண் தமிழ் மும்மை, the threefold Tamil of verse, song and drama), and the flood borrows its force from his horses, so river, king and Tamil are praised in one breath.

thinai_evidence.note: the river is praised through the king's own cavalry

comparisons.tenor: the Vaigai's flood spreading over its bed

tamil: மண் ஆர்ந்து இசைக்கும் முழவொடு கொண்ட தோள்
reading: Addressing a lovely woman whose shoulders keep time with the clay-smeared drum and fall in unison with it without her seeming to heed, the speaker asks whether the hearts of those who watch her can stay with them.
nuance: The syntax of lines 1 and 2 is open: கொண்ட தோள் may be her shoulders moving with the drum in a dance, or a man's drum-like shoulders into whose embrace she falls without a thought; on either reading the closing question turns her beauty into the onlookers' loss of heart, the love-at-sight that the fragment leaves without a named lover.

tamil: முன்பு உற்று அறியா முதல் புணர்ச்சி மொய் குழலை
இன்பு உற்று அணிந்த இயல் அணியும் வன் பணியும்
நாண் எனும் தொல்லை அணி என்ன நல்நுதலை ... ... ...னந்து
reading: At a first union she had never known before, the girl with thick tresses wore with joy her natural beauty and her strong jewels, and with them modesty, called her ancient ornament; the rest of the line is lost.
nuance: Three ornaments are ranked: the beauty she was born with (இயல் அணி), the jewels she put on (வன் பணி), and modesty, which is called older than both (தொல்லை அணி), so the shame that might seem to hold her back at the first union is counted as her oldest adornment.

thinai_evidence.note: the first union, never known before, is the kalavu meeting of kurinji

tamil: உலகம் ஒரு நிறையாத் தான் ஓர் நிறையாப்
புலவர் புலக் கோலால் தூக்க, உலகு அனைத்தும்
reading: When poets set the world in one pan and the city in the other and weighed them with the balance of their learning, the whole world drooped while the Pandya's four-towered Koodal stayed unfaded.
nuance: வாட does double work: in a balance the pan that goes down is the heavier, but வாடு is also to wither, so the world 'sinks' and 'fades' at once while Koodal, the one that does not fade (வாடாத), is praised for a permanence the scale cannot measure; the judges are poets, not kings.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the Pandya's city by a weighing that the poets make

comparisons.tenor: the poets' judgment as a balance beam

comparisons.vehicle: உலகம் ஒரு நிறையாத் தான் ஓர் நிறையா
comparisons.tenor: the world and the city as the two weights set against each other

tamil: தாது உண் பறவை அனையர், பரிசில் வாழ்நர்;
கோழியின் எழாது, எம் பேர் ஊர் துயிலே.
reading: Our great town is like the lotus that blossomed from Mayon's navel: its streets are the petals, the lord's palace the pericarp, its Tamil households the pollen and those who live on gifts the bees that eat it; it wakes from its safe sweet sleep only to the voices reciting the four Vedas born from the tongue of Brahma born in that flower, and not, like Vanji and Kozhi, to the cock's crow.
nuance: The flower is a map of a society: palace at the centre, households as the pollen that is the flower's wealth, and gift-seekers as the bees that feed on the households, not on the palace. The last lines pun on கோழி, the Chola city Uraiyur and the cock (line 11): the rival capitals wake to a bird, Madurai to the Veda, so the praise ranks the three capitals by the sound each wakes to.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the city laid out as one flower

comparisons.tenor: the lord's palace at the centre
the way the town wakes (by contrast)

reading: Can Madurai ever decline, rather than stand firm and blossom in fame throughout the Tamil land fenced by cool Tamil, as long as the hill of the king with the bannered chariot endures?
nuance: The land is fenced not by mountains or sea but by its language (தண் தமிழ் வேலி). This is the first of three fragments built on one frame (thirattu 9, 10, 11): each ends 'as long as the king's ... exists', and the measure moves from the hill to the river to his word. Whose hill is meant (the Pandya's, or the god's Parankundram) the fragment does not settle.

thinai_evidence.note: a blessing on the city's lasting fame

comparisons.tenor: Tamil as the boundary that encloses the Tamil land

reading: Like the tilaka drawn on the brow of the lady of fortune, matching her beauty, Madurai lights the world and blossoms in fame; can it ever prove false as long as the Vaigai of the king of the adorned chariot flows?
nuance: The world is the goddess's face and Madurai the mark at its centre: the simile makes the city the one point that gives the whole its auspiciousness, and பொய்யாதல் ('turning false') treats fame as a promise the city keeps.

thinai_evidence.note: a blessing on the city's lasting fame

comparisons.tenor: Madurai on the face of the world

reading: Like the heavy makara earring on the ear of Karthigai, Madurai shines in excellence and blossoms in prosperity; can any loss come to it as long as the word of the king of the bannered chariot stands?
nuance: கோத்தை is a rare word; its place in the frame, where the sister fragments have குன்றுதல் (decline) and பொய்யாதல் (proving false), fixes it as loss or defect. Karthigai is the asterism pictured as a woman, so the city is a jewel in the sky's ear. The third measure is வார்த்தை, the king's word or renown, so the city's endurance ends tied to speech rather than to hill or river.

thinai_evidence.note: a blessing on the city's lasting prosperity

reading: High-towered Koodal and the red Vel's Parankundram, which honour those who give and rejoice to see those who receive: those who live there are the ones rightly called living, and who among the rest would go to the world of the gods?
nuance: The city is praised for rejoicing at the sight of receivers (ஏற்பாரைப் பார்த்து உவக்கும்), not only at givers: asking is part of the honoured life, not its shame. Line 4 is compressed; it may ask who would go to the gods' world, or who among those not living there is going to it, but either way heaven is ranked below life in Koodal.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the city and the god's hill above heaven

tamil: செவ் வேற் கோ குன்றம் நுகர்தல் இனிதுகொல்?
வை வேல் நுதி அன்ன கண்ணார் துணையாக
reading: Is it sweeter to bathe in the Vaigai's rising flood, or to enjoy the hill of the king of the red spear, and how shall we spend it with women whose eyes are like the sharp spear's point as our companions? To be lost every day in such doubt about which way to go is the nature of tall-towered Koodal of Nediyon.
nuance: The praise is put as a complaint: the city has so many pleasures (river, sacred hill, women) that its people lose their way among them daily (வழி மயக்குற்று மருடல்). The love matter is the city's, not a lover's: no one is parted, and the choice of pleasures is itself the proof of Koodal's plenty. நெடியான் may be Thirumal or the Pandya.

thinai_evidence.note: the lovers' dilemma is offered as the nature of the city, a praise of Koodal
